## Create a New Certificate

<a id="opIdcertificates_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/certificates \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "web-cert-01",
    "type": "lets_encrypt",
    "dns_names": [
      "www.example.com",
      "example.com"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/certificates`

To upload new SSL certificate which you have previously generated, send a POST
request to `/v2/certificates`.

When uploading a user-generated certificate, the `private_key`,
`leaf_certificate`, and optionally the `certificate_chain` attributes should
be provided. The type must be set to `custom`.

When using Let's Encrypt to create a certificate, the `dns_names` attribute
must be provided, and the type must be set to `lets_encrypt`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "web-cert-01",
  "type": "lets_encrypt",
  "dns_names": [
    "www.example.com",
    "example.com"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-certificate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|A unique human-readable name referring to a certificate.|
|» type|body|string|false|A string representing the type of the certificate. The value will be `custom` for a user-uploaded certificate or `lets_encrypt` for one automatically generated with Let's Encrypt.|
|» dns_names|body|[string]|true|An array of fully qualified domain names (FQDNs) for which the certificate was issued. A certificate covering all subdomains can be issued using a wildcard (e.g. `*.example.com`).|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|A unique human-readable name referring to a certificate.|
|» type|body|string|false|A string representing the type of the certificate. The value will be `custom` for a user-uploaded certificate or `lets_encrypt` for one automatically generated with Let's Encrypt.|
|» certificate_chain|body|string|false|The full PEM-formatted trust chain between the certificate authority's certificate and your domain's SSL certificate.|
|» leaf_certificate|body|string|true|The contents of a PEM-formatted public SSL certificate.|
|» private_key|body|string|true|The contents of a PEM-formatted private-key corresponding to the SSL certificate.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|custom|
|» type|lets_encrypt|
|» type|custom|
|» type|lets_encrypt|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "certificate": {
    "created_at": "2017-02-08T16:02:37Z",
    "dns_names": [
      ""
    ],
    "id": "892071a0-bb95-49bc-8021-3afd67a210bf",
    "name": "web-cert-01",
    "not_after": "2017-02-22T00:23:00Z",
    "sha1_fingerprint": "dfcc9f57d86bf58e321c2c6c31c7a971be244ac7",
    "state": "verified",
    "type": "custom"
  }
}
```

The value of this will be an object that contains the standard attributes associated with a certificate.<br>When using Let's Encrypt, the initial value of the certificate's `state` attribute will be `pending`. When the certificate has been successfully issued by Let's Encrypt, this will transition to `verified` and be ready for use.|Inline|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-container-registry">Container Registry</h1>

DigitalOcean offers the ability for you to create a
[private container registry](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/images/container-registry/quickstart/)
to store your Docker images for use with your Kubernetes clusters. This
container registry runs inside the same datacenters as your cluster,
ensuring reliable and performant rollout of image deployments.

You can only create one registry per DigitalOcean account, but you can use
that registry to create as many repositories as you wish.

## Get Container Registry Information

<a id="opIdregistry_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/registry \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

## Create Container Registry

<a id="opIdregistry_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/registry \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "example",
    "region": "fra1",
    "subscription_tier_slug": "basic"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/registry`

To create your container registry, send a POST request to `/v2/registry`.

The `name` becomes part of the URL for images stored in the registry. For
example, if your registry is called `example`, an image in it will have the
URL `registry.digitalocean.com/example/image:tag`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "example",
  "region": "fra1",
  "subscription_tier_slug": "basic"
}
```

<h3 id="create-container-registry-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|A globally unique name for the container registry. Must be lowercase and be composed only of numbers, letters and `-`, up to a limit of 63 characters.|
|» region|body|string|false|Slug of the region where registry data is stored. When not provided, a region will be selected.|
|» subscription_tier_slug|body|string|true|The slug of the subscription tier to sign up for. Valid values can be retrieved using the options endpoint.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» region|nyc3|
|» region|sfo3|
|» region|ams3|
|» region|sgp1|
|» region|fra1|
|» subscription_tier_slug|starter|
|» subscription_tier_slug|basic|
|» subscription_tier_slug|professional|

```json
}
```

## Get Docker Credentials for Container Registry

<a id="opIdregistry_get_dockerCredentials"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/registry/docker-credentials \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/registry/docker-credentials`

In order to access your container registry with the Docker client or from a
Kubernetes cluster, you will need to configure authentication. The necessary
JSON configuration can be retrieved by sending a GET request to
`/v2/registry/docker-credentials`.

The response will be in the format of a Docker `config.json` file. To use the
config in your Kubernetes cluster, create a Secret with:

    kubectl create secret generic docr \
      --from-file=.dockerconfigjson=config.json \
      --type=kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson

By default, the returned credentials have read-only access to your registry
and cannot be used to push images. This is appropriate for most Kubernetes
clusters. To retrieve read/write credentials, suitable for use with the Docker
client or in a CI system, read_write may be provided as query parameter. For
example: `/v2/registry/docker-credentials?read_write=true`

By default, the returned credentials will not expire. To retrieve credentials
with an expiry set, expiry_seconds may be provided as a query parameter. For
example: `/v2/registry/docker-credentials?expiry_seconds=3600` will return
credentials that expire after one hour.


<h3 id="get-docker-credentials-for-container-registry-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|expiry_seconds|query|integer|false|The duration in seconds that the returned registry credentials will be valid. If not set or 0, the credentials will not expire.|
|read_write|query|boolean|false|By default, the registry credentials allow for read-only access. Set this query parameter to `true` to obtain read-write credentials.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "auths": {
    "registry.digitalocean.com": {
      "auth": "YjdkMDNhNjk0N2IyMTdlZmI2ZjNlYzNiZDM1MDQ1ODI6YjdkMDNhNjk0N2IyMTdlZmI2ZjNlYzNiZDM1MDQ1ODIK"
    }
  }
}
```

## List Registry Options (Subscription Tiers and Available Regions)

<a id="opIdregistry_get_options"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/registry/options \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/registry/options`

This endpoint serves to provide additional information as to which option values are available when creating a container registry.
There are multiple subscription tiers available for container registry. Each tier allows a different number of image repositories to be created in your registry, and has a different amount of storage and transfer included.
There are multiple regions available for container registry and controls where your data is stored.
To list the available options, send a GET request to `/v2/registry/options`.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "options": {
    "available_regions": [
      "nyc3",
      "sfo3",
      "ams3",
      "sgp1",
      "fra1"
    ],
    "subscription_tiers": [
      {
        "allow_storage_overage": false,
        "eligibility_reasons": [
          "OverRepositoryLimit"
        ],
        "eligible": false,
        "included_bandwidth_bytes": 524288000,
        "included_repositories": 1,
        "included_storage_bytes": 524288000,
        "monthly_price_in_cents": 0,
        "name": "Starter",
        "slug": "starter"
      },
      {
        "allow_storage_overage": true,
        "eligible": true,
        "included_bandwidth_bytes": 5368709120,
        "included_repositories": 5,
        "included_storage_bytes": 5368709120,
        "monthly_price_in_cents": 500,
        "name": "Basic",
        "slug": "basic"
      },
      {
        "allow_storage_overage": true,
        "eligible": true,
        "included_bandwidth_bytes": 107374182400,
        "included_repositories": 0,
        "included_storage_bytes": 107374182400,
        "monthly_price_in_cents": 2000,
        "name": "Professional",
        "slug": "professional"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Update Subscription Tier

<a id="opIdregistry_update_subscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/registry/subscription \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "tier_slug": "basic"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/registry/subscription`

After creating your registry, you can switch to a different subscription tier to better suit your needs. To do this, send a POST request to `/v2/registry/subscription`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "tier_slug": "basic"
}
```

|» tier_slug|starter|
|» tier_slug|basic|
|» tier_slug|professional|

## Validate a Container Registry Name

<a id="opIdregistry_validate_name"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/registry/validate-name \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "example"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/registry/validate-name`

To validate that a container registry name is available for use, send a POST
request to `/v2/registry/validate-name`.

If the name is both formatted correctly and available, the response code will
be 204 and contain no body. If the name is already in use, the response will
be a 409 Conflict.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "example"
}
```

<h3 id="validate-a-container-registry-name-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|A globally unique name for the container registry. Must be lowercase and be composed only of numbers, letters and `-`, up to a limit of 63 characters.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 409 Response

```json

  "id": "conflict",

}
```


> default Response

```json
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Start Garbage Collection

<a id="opIdregistry_run_garbageCollection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/registry/example/garbage-collection \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/registry/{registry_name}/garbage-collection`

Garbage collection enables users to clear out unreferenced blobs (layer &
manifest data) after deleting one or more manifests from a repository. If
there are no unreferenced blobs resulting from the deletion of one or more
manifests, garbage collection is effectively a noop.
[See here for more information](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/container-registry/how-to/clean-up-container-registry/)
about how and why you should clean up your container registry periodically.

To request a garbage collection run on your registry, send a POST request to
`/v2/registry/$REGISTRY_NAME/garbage-collection`. This will initiate the
following sequence of events on your registry.

* Set the registry to read-only mode, meaning no further write-scoped
  JWTs will be issued to registry clients. Existing write-scoped JWTs will
  continue to work until they expire which can take up to 15 minutes.
* Wait until all existing write-scoped JWTs have expired.
* Scan all registry manifests to determine which blobs are unreferenced.
* Delete all unreferenced blobs from the registry.
* Record the number of blobs deleted and bytes freed, mark the garbage
  collection status as `success`.
* Remove the read-only mode restriction from the registry, meaning write-scoped
  JWTs will once again be issued to registry clients.


<h3 id="start-garbage-collection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|registry_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "garbage_collection": {
    "blobs_deleted": 42,
    "created_at": "2020-10-30T21:03:24Z",
    "freed_bytes": 667,
    "registry_name": "example",
    "status": "requested",
    "updated_at": "2020-10-30T21:03:44Z",
    "uuid": "eff0feee-49c7-4e8f-ba5c-a320c109c8a8"
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The response will be a JSON object with a key of `garbage_collection`. This will be a json object with attributes representing the currently-active garbage collection.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|Inline|

## Update Garbage Collection

<a id="opIdregistry_update_garbageCollection"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/registry/example/garbage-collection/eff0feee-49c7-4e8f-ba5c-a320c109c8a8 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "cancel": true
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/registry/{registry_name}/garbage-collection/{garbage_collection_uuid}`

To cancel the currently-active garbage collection for a registry, send a PUT request to `/v2/registry/$REGISTRY_NAME/garbage-collection/$GC_UUID` and specify one or more of the attributes below.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "cancel": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-garbage-collection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|registry_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry.|
|garbage_collection_uuid|path|string|true|The UUID of a garbage collection run.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» cancel|body|boolean|false|A boolean value indicating that the garbage collection should be cancelled.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

    "updated_at": "2020-10-30T21:03:44Z",
```

## List All Container Registry Repository Manifests

<a id="opIdregistry_list_repositoryManifests"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/registry/example/repo-1/digests \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/registry/{registry_name}/{repository_name}/digests`

To list all manifests in your container registry repository, send a GET
request to `/v2/registry/$REGISTRY_NAME/repositories/$REPOSITORY_NAME/digests`.

Note that if your repository name contains `/` characters, it must be
URL-encoded in the request URL. For example, to list manifests for
`registry.digitalocean.com/example/my/repo`, the path would be
`/v2/registry/example/repositories/my%2Frepo/digests`.


<h3 id="list-all-container-registry-repository-manifests-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|
|registry_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry.|
|repository_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry repository. If the name contains `/` characters, they must be URL-encoded, e.g. `%2F`.|

## Delete Container Registry Repository Manifest

<a id="opIdregistry_delete_repositoryManifest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/registry/example/repo-1/digests/sha256%3Acb8a924afdf0229ef7515d9e5b3024e23b3eb03ddbba287f4a19c6ac90b8d221 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/registry/{registry_name}/{repository_name}/digests/{manifest_digest}`

To delete a container repository manifest by digest, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/registry/$REGISTRY_NAME/repositories/$REPOSITORY_NAME/digests/$MANIFEST_DIGEST`.

Note that if your repository name contains `/` characters, it must be
URL-encoded in the request URL. For example, to delete
`registry.digitalocean.com/example/my/repo@sha256:abcd`, the path would be
`/v2/registry/example/repositories/my%2Frepo/digests/sha256:abcd`.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully.


<h3 id="delete-container-registry-repository-manifest-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|registry_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry.|
|repository_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry repository. If the name contains `/` characters, they must be URL-encoded, e.g. `%2F`.|
|manifest_digest|path|string|true|The manifest digest of a container registry repository tag.|

```json
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."

}
```

## List All Container Registry Repository Tags

<a id="opIdregistry_list_repositoryTags"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/registry/example/repo-1/tags \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/registry/{registry_name}/{repository_name}/tags`

To list all tags in your container registry repository, send a GET
request to `/v2/registry/$REGISTRY_NAME/repositories/$REPOSITORY_NAME/tags`.

Note that if your repository name contains `/` characters, it must be
URL-encoded in the request URL. For example, to list tags for
`registry.digitalocean.com/example/my/repo`, the path would be
`/v2/registry/example/repositories/my%2Frepo/tags`.

|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|
|registry_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry.|
|repository_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry repository. If the name contains `/` characters, they must be URL-encoded, e.g. `%2F`.|

## Delete Container Registry Repository Tag

<a id="opIdregistry_delete_repositoryTag"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/registry/example/repo-1/tags/06a447a \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/registry/{registry_name}/{repository_name}/tags/{repository_tag}`

To delete a container repository tag, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/registry/$REGISTRY_NAME/repositories/$REPOSITORY_NAME/tags/$TAG`.

Note that if your repository name contains `/` characters, it must be
URL-encoded in the request URL. For example, to delete
`registry.digitalocean.com/example/my/repo:mytag`, the path would be
`/v2/registry/example/repositories/my%2Frepo/tags/mytag`.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully.


<h3 id="delete-container-registry-repository-tag-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|registry_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry.|
|repository_name|path|string|true|The name of a container registry repository. If the name contains `/` characters, they must be URL-encoded, e.g. `%2F`.|
|repository_tag|path|string|true|The name of a container registry repository tag.|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-databases">Databases</h1>

DigitalOcean's [managed database service](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/databases)
simplifies the creation and management of highly available database clusters. Currently, it
offers support for [PostgreSQL](http://www.digitalocean.com/docs/databases/postgresql/),
[Redis](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/databases/redis/),
[MySQL](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/databases/mysql/), and
[MongoDB](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/databases/mongodb/).

By sending requests to the `/v2/databases` endpoint, you can list, create, or delete
database clusters as well as scale the size of a cluster, add or remove read-only replicas,
and manage other configuration details.

Database clusters may be deployed in a multi-node, high-availability configuration.
If your machine type is above the basic nodes, your node plan is above the smallest option,
or you are running MongoDB, you may additionally include up to two standby nodes in your cluster.

The size of individual nodes in a database cluster is represented by a human-readable slug,
which is used in some of the following requests. Each slug denotes the node's identifier,
CPU count, and amount of RAM, in that order.

For **Basic nodes**, reference the following table for its slug:

Slug               | CPU     | RAM
-------------------|---------|---------
db-s-1vcpu-1gb     | 1 vCPU  | 1 GB
db-s-1vcpu-2gb     | 1 vCPU  | 2 GB
db-s-2vcpu-4gb     | 2 vCPU  | 4 GB
db-s-4vcpu-8gb     | 4 vCPU  | 8 GB
db-s-6vcpu-16gb    | 6 vCPU  | 16 GB
db-s-8vcpu-32gb    | 8 vCPU  | 32 GB
db-s-16vcpu-64gb   | 16 vCPU | 64 GB

For **General Purpose nodes**, reference the following table for its slug:

Slug               | CPU     | RAM
-------------------|---------|---------

gd-4vcpu-16gb      | 4 vCPU  | 16 GB
gd-8vcpu-32gb      | 8 vCPU  | 32 GB
gd-16vcpu-64gb     | 16 vCPU | 64 GB
gd-32vcpu-128gb    | 32 vCPU | 128 GB
gd-40vcpu-160gb    | 40 vCPU | 160 GB

-------------------|---------|---------

## List All Database Clusters

<a id="opIddatabases_list_clusters"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/databases`

To list all of the database clusters available on your account, send a GET request to `/v2/databases`. To limit the results to database clusters with a specific tag, include the `tag_name` query parameter set to the name of the tag. For example, `/v2/databases?tag_name=$TAG_NAME`.
The result will be a JSON object with a `databases` key. This will be set to an array of database objects, each of which will contain the standard database attributes.
The embedded `connection` and `private_connection` objects will contain the information needed to access the database cluster:
The embedded `maintenance_window` object will contain information about any scheduled maintenance for the database cluster.

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tag_name|query|string|false|Limits the results to database clusters with a specific tag.|

## Create a New Database Cluster

<a id="opIddatabases_create_cluster"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "engine": "pg",
    "name": "backend",
    "num_nodes": 2,
    "region": "nyc3",
    "size": "db-s-2vcpu-4gb",
    "tags": [
      "production"
    ],
    "version": "14"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/databases`

To create a database cluster, send a POST request to `/v2/databases`.
The response will be a JSON object with a key called `database`. The value of this will be an object that contains the standard attributes associated with a database cluster. The initial value of the database cluster's `status` attribute will be `creating`. When the cluster is ready to receive traffic, this will transition to `online`.
The embedded `connection` and `private_connection` objects will contain the information needed to access the database cluster.
DigitalOcean managed PostgreSQL and MySQL database clusters take automated daily backups. To create a new database cluster based on a backup of an existing cluster, send a POST request to `/v2/databases`. In addition to the standard database cluster attributes, the JSON body must include a key named `backup_restore` with the name of the original database cluster and the timestamp of the backup to be restored. Creating a database from a backup is the same as forking a database in the control panel.
Note: Backups are not supported for Redis clusters.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "engine": "pg",
  "name": "backend",
  "num_nodes": 2,
  "region": "nyc3",
  "size": "db-s-2vcpu-4gb",
  "tags": [
    "production"
  ],
  "version": "14"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-database-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» connection|body|object|false|none|
|» engine|body|string|true|A slug representing the database engine used for the cluster. The possible values are: "pg" for PostgreSQL, "mysql" for MySQL, "redis" for Redis, and "mongodb" for MongoDB.|
|» maintenance_window|body|object|false|none|
|» » day|body|string|true|The day of the week on which to apply maintenance updates.|
|» » hour|body|string|true|The hour in UTC at which maintenance updates will be applied in 24 hour format.|
|» name|body|string|true|A unique, human-readable name referring to a database cluster.|
|» num_nodes|body|integer|true|The number of nodes in the database cluster.|
|» private_connection|body|object|false|none|
|» private_network_uuid|body|string|false|A string specifying the UUID of the VPC to which the database cluster will be assigned. If excluded, the cluster when creating a new database cluster, it will be assigned to your account's default VPC for the region.|
|» project_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The ID of the project that the database cluster is assigned to. If excluded when creating a new database cluster, it will be assigned to your default project.|
|» region|body|string|true|The slug identifier for the region where the database cluster is located.|
|» rules|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » cluster_uuid|body|string|false|A unique ID for the database cluster to which the rule is applied.|
|» » type|body|string|true|The type of resource that the firewall rule allows to access the database cluster.|
|» » uuid|body|string|false|A unique ID for the firewall rule itself.|
|» » value|body|string|true|The ID of the specific resource, the name of a tag applied to a group of resources, or the IP address that the firewall rule allows to access the database cluster.|
|» size|body|string|true|The slug identifier representing the size of the nodes in the database cluster.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|An array of tags that have been applied to the database cluster.|
|» version|body|string|false|A string representing the version of the database engine in use for the cluster.|
|» backup_restore|body|object|false|none|
|» » backup_created_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp of an existing database cluster backup in ISO8601 combined date and time format. The most recent backup will be used if excluded.|
|» » database_name|body|string|true|The name of an existing database cluster from which the backup will be restored.|

## Retrieve an Existing Database Cluster

<a id="opIddatabases_get_cluster"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}`

To show information about an existing database cluster, send a GET request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID`.
The response will be a JSON object with a database key. This will be set to an object containing the standard database cluster attributes.
The embedded connection and private_connection objects will contain the information needed to access the database cluster.
The embedded maintenance_window object will contain information about any scheduled maintenance for the database cluster.

<h3 id="retrieve-an-existing-database-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|

## Destroy a Database Cluster

<a id="opIddatabases_destroy_cluster"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}`

To destroy a specific database, send a DELETE request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID`.
A status of 204 will be given. This indicates that the request was processed successfully, but that no response body is needed.

<h3 id="destroy-a-database-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## List Backups for a Database Cluster

<a id="opIddatabases_list_backups"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/backups \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/backups`

To list all of the available backups of a PostgreSQL or MySQL database cluster, send a GET request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/backups`.
**Note**: Backups are not supported for Redis clusters.
The result will be a JSON object with a `backups key`. This will be set to an array of backup objects, each of which will contain the size of the backup and the timestamp at which it was created.

<h3 id="list-backups-for-a-database-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "backups": [
    {
      "created_at": "2019-01-11T18:42:27Z",
      "size_gigabytes": 0.03357696
    },
    {
      "created_at": "2019-01-12T18:42:29Z",
      "size_gigabytes": 0.03364864
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h3 id="list-backups-for-a-database-cluster-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A JSON object with a key of `database_backups`.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|Inline|
|404|Not Found|The resource was not found.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|API Rate limit exceeded|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error.|Inline|
|default|Default|Unexpected error|Inline|

<h3 id="list-backups-for-a-database-cluster-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|backups|[object]|true|none|none|
|» created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|A time value given in ISO8601 combined date and time format at which the backup was created.|

## Retrieve the Public Certificate

<a id="opIddatabases_get_ca"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/ca \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/ca`

To retrieve the public certificate used to secure the connection to the database cluster send a GET request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/ca`.

The response will be a JSON object with a `ca` key. This will be set to an object
containing the base64 encoding of the public key certificate.


<h3 id="retrieve-the-public-certificate-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "ca": {
    "certificate": ""
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Retrieve an Existing Database Cluster Configuration

<a id="opIddatabases_get_config"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/config \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/config`

Shows configuration parameters for an existing database cluster by sending a GET request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/config`.
The response is a JSON object with a `config` key, which is set to an object
containing any database configuration parameters.


<h3 id="retrieve-an-existing-database-cluster-configuration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "config": {
    "sql_mode": "ANSI,ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION,NO_ZERO_DATE,NO_ZERO_IN_DATE,STRICT_ALL_TABLES",
    "sql_require_primary_key": true
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-an-existing-database-cluster-configuration-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A JSON object with a key of `config`.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|Inline|
|404|Not Found|The resource was not found.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|API Rate limit exceeded|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error.|Inline|
|default|Default|Unexpected error|Inline|

## Update the Database Configuration for an Existing Database

<a id="opIddatabases_patch_config"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/config \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "config": {
      "sql_mode": "ANSI,ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION,NO_ZERO_DATE,NO_ZERO_IN_DATE,STRICT_ALL_TABLES",
      "sql_require_primary_key": true
    }
  }'
```

`PATCH /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/config`

To update the configuration for an existing database cluster, send a PATCH request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/config`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "config": {
    "sql_mode": "ANSI,ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION,NO_ZERO_DATE,NO_ZERO_IN_DATE,STRICT_ALL_TABLES",
    "sql_require_primary_key": true
  }
}
```

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/dbs`

To list all of the databases in a clusters, send a GET request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/dbs`.

The result will be a JSON object with a `dbs` key. This will be set to an array
of database objects, each of which will contain the standard database attributes.

Note: Database management is not supported for Redis clusters.

## Add a New Database

<a id="opIddatabases_add"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/dbs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "alpha"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/dbs`

To add a new database to an existing cluster, send a POST request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/dbs`.

Note: Database management is not supported for Redis clusters.

The response will be a JSON object with a key called `db`. The value of this will be
an object that contains the standard attributes associated with a database.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "alpha"
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-new-database-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the database.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "db": {
    "name": "alpha"
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json

  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```


`DELETE /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/dbs/{database_name}`

To delete a specific database, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/dbs/$DB_NAME`.

A status of 204 will be given. This indicates that the request was processed
successfully, but that no response body is needed.

Note: Database management is not supported for Redis clusters.

## Retrieve the Eviction Policy for a Redis Cluster

<a id="opIddatabases_get_evictionPolicy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/eviction_policy \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/eviction_policy`

To retrieve the configured eviction policy for an existing Redis cluster, send a GET request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/eviction_policy`.
The response will be a JSON object with an `eviction_policy` key. This will be set to a string representing the eviction policy.

<h3 id="retrieve-the-eviction-policy-for-a-redis-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "eviction_policy": "allkeys_lru"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-the-eviction-policy-for-a-redis-cluster-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A JSON string with a key of `eviction_policy`.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|Inline|
|404|Not Found|The resource was not found.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|API Rate limit exceeded|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error.|Inline|
|default|Default|Unexpected error|Inline|

<h3 id="retrieve-the-eviction-policy-for-a-redis-cluster-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|eviction_policy|string|true|none|A string specifying the desired eviction policy for the Redis cluster.<br><br>- `noeviction`: Don't evict any data, returns error when memory limit is reached.<br>- `allkeys_lru:` Evict any key, least recently used (LRU) first.<br>- `allkeys_random`: Evict keys in a random order.<br>- `volatile_lru`: Evict keys with expiration only, least recently used (LRU) first.<br>- `volatile_random`: Evict keys with expiration only in a random order.<br>- `volatile_ttl`: Evict keys with expiration only, shortest time-to-live (TTL) first.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|eviction_policy|noeviction|
|eviction_policy|allkeys_lru|
|eviction_policy|allkeys_random|
|eviction_policy|volatile_lru|
|eviction_policy|volatile_random|
|eviction_policy|volatile_ttl|

## Configure the Eviction Policy for a Redis Cluster

<a id="opIddatabases_update_evictionPolicy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/eviction_policy \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "eviction_policy": "allkeys_lru"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/eviction_policy`

To configure an eviction policy for an existing Redis cluster, send a PUT request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/eviction_policy` specifying the desired policy.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "eviction_policy": "allkeys_lru"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» eviction_policy|body|string|true|A string specifying the desired eviction policy for the Redis cluster.<br><br>- `noeviction`: Don't evict any data, returns error when memory limit is reached.<br>- `allkeys_lru:` Evict any key, least recently used (LRU) first.<br>- `allkeys_random`: Evict keys in a random order.<br>- `volatile_lru`: Evict keys with expiration only, least recently used (LRU) first.<br>- `volatile_random`: Evict keys with expiration only in a random order.<br>- `volatile_ttl`: Evict keys with expiration only, shortest time-to-live (TTL) first.|

## List Firewall Rules (Trusted Sources) for a Database Cluster

<a id="opIddatabases_list_firewall_rules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/firewall \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/firewall`

To list all of a database cluster's firewall rules (known as "trusted sources" in the control panel), send a GET request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/firewall`.
The result will be a JSON object with a `rules` key.

<h3 id="list-firewall-rules-trusted-sources-for-a-database-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|

## Update Firewall Rules (Trusted Sources) for a Database

<a id="opIddatabases_update_firewall_rules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/firewall \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "rules": [
      {
        "type": "ip_addr",
        "value": "192.168.1.1"
      },
      {
        "type": "k8s",
        "value": "ff2a6c52-5a44-4b63-b99c-0e98e7a63d61"
      },
      {
        "type": "droplet",
        "value": "163973392"
      },
      {
        "type": "tag",
        "value": "backend"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/firewall`

To update a database cluster's firewall rules (known as "trusted sources" in the control panel), send a PUT request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/firewall` specifying which resources should be able to open connections to the database. You may limit connections to specific Droplets, Kubernetes clusters, or IP addresses. When a tag is provided, any Droplet or Kubernetes node with that tag applied to it will have access. The firewall is limited to 100 rules (or trusted sources). When possible, we recommend [placing your databases into a VPC network](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/networking/vpc/) to limit access to them instead of using a firewall.
A successful

```json
    {
      "type": "ip_addr",

    },

    },
    {
      "type": "tag",

    }

}
```

## Configure a Database Cluster's Maintenance Window

<a id="opIddatabases_update_maintenanceWindow"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/maintenance \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "day": "tuesday",
    "hour": "14:00"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/maintenance`

To configure the window when automatic maintenance should be performed for a database cluster, send a PUT request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/maintenance`.
A successful request will receive a 204 No Content status code with no body in response.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "day": "tuesday",
  "hour": "14:00"
}
```

<h3 id="configure-a-database-clusters-maintenance-window-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|body|body|object \| null|true|none|
|» day|body|string|true|The day of the week on which to apply maintenance updates.|
|» hour|body|string|true|The hour in UTC at which maintenance updates will be applied in 24 hour format.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

## Migrate a Database Cluster to a New Region

<a id="opIddatabases_update_region"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/migrate \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "region": "lon1"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/migrate`

To migrate a database cluster to a new region, send a `PUT` request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/migrate`. The body of the request must specify a
`region` attribute.

A successful request will receive a 202 Accepted status code with no body in
response. Querying the database cluster will show that its `status` attribute
will now be set to `migrating`. This will transition back to `online` when the
migration has completed.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "region": "lon1"
}
```

<h3 id="migrate-a-database-cluster-to-a-new-region-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» region|body|string|true|A slug identifier for the region to which the database cluster will be migrated.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h3 id="migrate-a-database-cluster-to-a-new-region-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|The does not indicate the success or failure of any operation, just that the request has been accepted for processing.|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|Inline|
|404|Not Found|The resource was not found.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|API Rate limit exceeded|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error.|Inline|
|default|Default|Unexpected error|Inline|

## Start an Online Migration

<a id="opIddatabases_update_onlineMigration"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/online-migration \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "disable_ssl": false,
    "source": {
      "dbname": "defaultdb",
      "host": "source-do-user-6607903-0.b.db.ondigitalocean.com",
      "password": "paakjnfe10rsrsmf",
      "port": 25060,
      "username": "doadmin"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/online-migration`

To start an online migration, send a PUT request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/online-migration` endpoint. Migrating a cluster establishes a connection with an existing cluster and replicates its contents to the target cluster. Online migration is only available for MySQL, PostgreSQL, and Redis clusters.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "disable_ssl": false,
  "source": {
    "dbname": "defaultdb",
    "host": "source-do-user-6607903-0.b.db.ondigitalocean.com",
    "password": "paakjnfe10rsrsmf",
    "port": 25060,
    "username": "doadmin"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="start-an-online-migration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» disable_ssl|body|boolean|false|Enables SSL encryption when connecting to the source database.|
|» source|body|object|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "created_at": "2020-10-29T15:57:38Z",
  "id": "77b28fc8-19ff-11eb-8c9c-c68e24557488",
  "status": "running"
}
```

`DELETE /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/online-migration/{migration_id}`

To stop an online migration, send a DELETE request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/online-migration/$MIGRATION_ID`.

A status of 204 will be given. This indicates that the request was processed successfully, but that no response body is needed.

<a id="opIddatabases_list_connectionPools"></a>


`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/pools`

To list all of the connection pools available to a PostgreSQL database cluster, send a GET request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/pools`.
The result will be a JSON object with a `pools` key. This will be set to an array of connection pool objects.

<h3 id="list-connection-pools-postgresql-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|

## Add a New Connection Pool (PostgreSQL)

<a id="opIddatabases_add_connectionPool"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/pools \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "db": "defaultdb",
    "mode": "transaction",
    "name": "backend-pool",
    "size": 10,
    "user": "doadmin"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/pools`

For PostgreSQL database clusters, connection pools can be used to allow a
database to share its idle connections. The popular PostgreSQL connection
pooling utility PgBouncer is used to provide this service. [See here for more information](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/databases/postgresql/how-to/manage-connection-pools/)
about how and why to use PgBouncer connection pooling including
details about the available transaction modes.

To add a new connection pool to a PostgreSQL database cluster, send a POST
request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/pools` specifying a name for the pool,
the user to connect with, the database to connect to, as well as its desired
size and transaction mode.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "db": "defaultdb",
  "mode": "transaction",
  "name": "backend-pool",
  "size": 10,
  "user": "doadmin"
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-new-connection-pool-postgresql-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» connection|body|object|false|none|
|» db|body|string|true|The database for use with the connection pool.|
|» mode|body|string|true|The PGBouncer transaction mode for the connection pool. The allowed values are session, transaction, and statement.|
|» name|body|string|true|A unique name for the connection pool. Must be between 3 and 60 characters.|
|» private_connection|body|object|false|none|
|» size|body|integer(int32)|true|The desired size of the PGBouncer connection pool. The maximum allowed size is determined by the size of the cluster's primary node. 25 backend server connections are allowed for every 1GB of RAM. Three are reserved for maintenance. For example, a primary node with 1 GB of RAM allows for a maximum of 22 backend server connections while one with 4 GB would allow for 97. Note that these are shared across all connection pools in a cluster.|
|» user|body|string|false|The name of the user for use with the connection pool. When excluded, all sessions connect to the database as the inbound user.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "pool": {
    "connection": {
      "database": "backend-pool",
      "host": "backend-do-user-19081923-0.db.ondigitalocean.com",
      "password": "wv78n3zpz42xezdk",
      "port": 25061,
      "ssl": true,
      "uri": "postgres://doadmin:wv78n3zpz42xezdk@backend-do-user-19081923-0.db.ondigitalocean.com:25061/backend-pool?sslmode=require",
      "user": "doadmin"
    },
    "db": "defaultdb",
    "mode": "transaction",
    "name": "backend-pool",
    "size": 10,
    "user": "doadmin"
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response


`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/pools/{pool_name}`

To show information about an existing connection pool for a PostgreSQL database cluster, send a GET request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/pools/$POOL_NAME`.
The response will be a JSON object with a `pool` key.

## Update Connection Pools (PostgreSQL)

<a id="opIddatabases_update_connectionPool"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/pools/backend-pool \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "db": "defaultdb",
    "mode": "transaction",
    "size": 10,
    "user": "doadmin"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/pools/{pool_name}`

To update a connection pool for a PostgreSQL database cluster, send a PUT request to  `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/pools/$POOL_NAME`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "db": "defaultdb",
  "mode": "transaction",
  "size": 10,
  "user": "doadmin"
}
```

<h3 id="update-connection-pools-postgresql-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|pool_name|path|string|true|The name used to identify the connection pool.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» db|body|string|true|The database for use with the connection pool.|
|» mode|body|string|true|The PGBouncer transaction mode for the connection pool. The allowed values are session, transaction, and statement.|
|» size|body|integer(int32)|true|The desired size of the PGBouncer connection pool. The maximum allowed size is determined by the size of the cluster's primary node. 25 backend server connections are allowed for every 1GB of RAM. Three are reserved for maintenance. For example, a primary node with 1 GB of RAM allows for a maximum of 22 backend server connections while one with 4 GB would allow for 97. Note that these are shared across all connection pools in a cluster.|
|» user|body|string|false|The name of the user for use with the connection pool. When excluded, all sessions connect to the database as the inbound user.|

```json
  "id": "unauthorized",

```

```json
}
```

## Delete a Connection Pool (PostgreSQL)

<a id="opIddatabases_delete_connectionPool"></a>


`DELETE /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/pools/{pool_name}`

To delete a specific connection pool for a PostgreSQL database cluster, send
a DELETE request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/pools/$POOL_NAME`.

A status of 204 will be given. This indicates that the request was processed
successfully, but that no response body is needed.

## List All Read-only Replicas

<a id="opIddatabases_list_replicas"></a>

> Code samples

```bash

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/replicas`

To list all of the read-only replicas associated with a database cluster, send a GET request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/replicas`.

**Note**: Read-only replicas are not supported for Redis clusters.

The result will be a JSON object with a `replicas` key. This will be set to an array of database replica objects, each of which will contain the standard database replica attributes.

## Create a Read-only Replica

<a id="opIddatabases_create_replica"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/replicas \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "read-nyc3-01",
    "region": "nyc3",
    "size": "db-s-2vcpu-4gb"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/replicas`

To create a read-only replica for a PostgreSQL or MySQL database cluster, send a POST request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/replicas` specifying the name it should be given, the size of the node to be used, and the region where it will be located.

**Note**: Read-only replicas are not supported for Redis clusters.

The response will be a JSON object with a key called `replica`. The value of this will be an object that contains the standard attributes associated with a database replica. The initial value of the read-only replica's `status` attribute will be `forking`. When the replica is ready to receive traffic, this will transition to `active`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "read-nyc3-01",
  "region": "nyc3",
  "size": "db-s-2vcpu-4gb"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-read-only-replica-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» connection|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name to give the read-only replicating|
|» private_connection|body|object|false|none|
|» private_network_uuid|body|string|false|A string specifying the UUID of the VPC to which the read-only replica will be assigned. If excluded, the replica will be assigned to your account's default VPC for the region.|
|» region|body|string|false|A slug identifier for the region where the read-only replica will be located. If excluded, the replica will be placed in the same region as the cluster.|
|» size|body|string|true|A slug identifier representing the size of the node for the read-only replica. The size of the replica must be at least as large as the node size for the database cluster from which it is replicating.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|A flat array of tag names as strings to apply to the read-only replica after it is created. Tag names can either be existing or new tags.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "replica": {
    "connection": {
      "database": "defaultdb",
      "host": "read-nyc3-01-do-user-19081923-0.db.ondigitalocean.com",
      "password": "wv78n3zpz42xezdk",
      "port": 25060,
      "ssl": true,
      "uri": "",
      "user": "doadmin"
    },
    "created_at": "2019-01-11T18:37:36Z",
    "name": "read-nyc3-01",
    "private_connection": {
      "database": "",
      "host": "private-read-nyc3-01-do-user-19081923-0.db.ondigitalocean.com",
      "password": "wv78n3zpz42xezdk",
```

## Retrieve an Existing Read-only Replica

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/replicas/{replica_name}`

To show information about an existing database replica, send a GET request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/replicas/$REPLICA_NAME`.

**Note**: Read-only replicas are not supported for Redis clusters.

The response will be a JSON object with a `replica key`. This will be set to an object containing the standard database replica attributes.

## Destroy a Read-only Replica

```bash
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/replicas/{replica_name}`

To destroy a specific read-only replica, send a DELETE request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/replicas/$REPLICA_NAME`.

**Note**: Read-only replicas are not supported for Redis clusters.

A status of 204 will be given. This indicates that the request was processed successfully, but that no response body is needed.

## Promote a Read-only Replica to become a Primary Cluster

<a id="opIddatabases_promote_replica"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/replicas/read-nyc3-01/promote \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/replicas/{replica_name}/promote`

To promote a specific read-only replica, send a PUT request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/replicas/$REPLICA_NAME/promote`.

**Note**: Read-only replicas are not supported for Redis clusters.

A status of 204 will be given. This indicates that the request was processed successfully, but that no response body is needed.

<h3 id="promote-a-read-only-replica-to-become-a-primary-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|replica_name|path|string|true|The name of the database replica.|

## Resize a Database Cluster

<a id="opIddatabases_update_clusterSize"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/resize \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "num_nodes": 3,
    "size": "db-s-4vcpu-8gb"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/resize`

To resize a database cluster, send a PUT request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/resize`. The body of the request must specify both the size and num_nodes attributes.
A successful request will receive a 202 Accepted status code with no body in response. Querying the database cluster will show that its status attribute will now be set to resizing. This will transition back to online when the resize operation has completed.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "num_nodes": 3,
  "size": "db-s-4vcpu-8gb"
}
```

<h3 id="resize-a-database-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» num_nodes|body|integer(int32)|true|The number of nodes in the database cluster. Valid values are are 1-3. In addition to the primary node, up to two standby nodes may be added for highly available configurations.|
|» size|body|string|true|A slug identifier representing desired the size of the nodes in the database cluster.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|Inline|

## Retrieve the SQL Modes for a MySQL Cluster

<a id="opIddatabases_get_sql_mode"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/sql_mode \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/sql_mode`

To retrieve the configured SQL modes for an existing MySQL cluster, send a GET request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/sql_mode`.
The response will be a JSON object with a `sql_mode` key. This will be set to a string representing the configured SQL modes.

## Update SQL Mode for a Cluster

<a id="opIddatabases_update_sql_mode"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/sql_mode \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "sql_mode": "ANSI,ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION,NO_ZERO_DATE,NO_ZERO_IN_DATE"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/sql_mode`

To configure the SQL modes for an existing MySQL cluster, send a PUT request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/sql_mode` specifying the desired modes. See the official MySQL 8 documentation for a [full list of supported SQL modes](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/sql-mode.html#sql-mode-full).
A successful request will receive a 204 No Content status code with no body in response.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "sql_mode": "ANSI,ERROR_FOR_DIVISION_BY_ZERO,NO_ENGINE_SUBSTITUTION,NO_ZERO_DATE,NO_ZERO_IN_DATE"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» sql_mode|body|string|true|A string specifying the configured SQL modes for the MySQL cluster.|

## Upgrade Major Version for a Database

<a id="opIddatabases_update_major_version"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/upgrade \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "version": "14"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/upgrade`

To upgrade the major version of a database, send a PUT request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/upgrade`, specifying the target version.
A successful request will receive a 204 No Content status code with no body in response.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "version": "14"
}
```

## List all Database Users

<a id="opIddatabases_list_users"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/users \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/users`

To list all of the users for your database cluster, send a GET request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/users`.

Note: User management is not supported for Redis clusters.

The result will be a JSON object with a `users` key. This will be set to an array
of database user objects, each of which will contain the standard database user attributes.

For MySQL clusters, additional options will be contained in the mysql_settings object.


<h3 id="list-all-database-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "users": [
    {
      "name": "app-01",
      "password": "jge5lfxtzhx42iff",
      "role": "normal"
    },
    {
      "name": "doadmin",
      "password": "wv78n3zpz42xezd",
      "role": "primary"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

|429|Too Many Requests|API Rate limit exceeded|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error.|Inline|

## Add a Database User

<a id="opIddatabases_add_user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/users \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "app-01"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/users`

To add a new database user, send a POST request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/users`
with the desired username.

Note: User management is not supported for Redis clusters.

When adding a user to a MySQL cluster, additional options can be configured in the
`mysql_settings` object.

The response will be a JSON object with a key called `user`. The value of this will be an
object that contains the standard attributes associated with a database user including
its randomly generated password.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "app-01"
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-database-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» mysql_settings|body|object|false|none|
|» » auth_plugin|body|string|true|A string specifying the authentication method to be used for connections<br>to the MySQL user account. The valid values are `mysql_native_password`<br>or `caching_sha2_password`. If excluded when creating a new user, the<br>default for the version of MySQL in use will be used. As of MySQL 8.0, the<br>default is `caching_sha2_password`.<br>|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of a database user.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » auth_plugin|mysql_native_password|
|» » auth_plugin|caching_sha2_password|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "user": {
    "name": "app-01",
    "password": "jge5lfxtzhx42iff",
    "role": "normal"
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-database-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|A JSON object with a key of `user`.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|Inline|
|404|Not Found|The resource was not found.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|API Rate limit exceeded|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error.|Inline|
|default|Default|Unexpected error|Inline|

## Retrieve an Existing Database User

<a id="opIddatabases_get_user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/users/app-01 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/users/{username}`

To show information about an existing database user, send a GET request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/users/$USERNAME`.

Note: User management is not supported for Redis clusters.

The response will be a JSON object with a `user` key. This will be set to an object
containing the standard database user attributes.

For MySQL clusters, additional options will be contained in the mysql_settings
object.

## Remove a Database User

<a id="opIddatabases_delete_user"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/users/app-01 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/users/{username}`

To remove a specific database user, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/users/$USERNAME`.

A status of 204 will be given. This indicates that the request was processed
successfully, but that no response body is needed.

Note: User management is not supported for Redis clusters.


<h3 id="remove-a-database-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|username|path|string|true|The name of the database user.|

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

## Reset a Database User's Password or Authentication Method

<a id="opIddatabases_reset_auth"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/databases/9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30/users/app-01/reset_auth \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "mysql_settings": {
      "auth_plugin": "caching_sha2_password"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v2/databases/{database_cluster_uuid}/users/{username}/reset_auth`

To reset the password for a database user, send a POST request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/users/$USERNAME/reset_auth`.

For `mysql` databases, the authentication method can be specifying by
including a key in the JSON body called `mysql_settings` with the `auth_plugin`
value specified.

The response will be a JSON object with a `user` key. This will be set to an
object containing the standard database user attributes.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "mysql_settings": {
    "auth_plugin": "caching_sha2_password"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="reset-a-database-users-password-or-authentication-method-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|database_cluster_uuid|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a database cluster.|
|username|path|string|true|The name of the database user.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» mysql_settings|body|object|false|none|
|» » auth_plugin|body|string|true|A string specifying the authentication method to be used for connections<br>to the MySQL user account. The valid values are `mysql_native_password`<br>or `caching_sha2_password`. If excluded when creating a new user, the<br>default for the version of MySQL in use will be used. As of MySQL 8.0, the<br>default is `caching_sha2_password`.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » auth_plugin|mysql_native_password|
|» » auth_plugin|caching_sha2_password|

> Example responses

```json
    "name": "app-01",
    "password": "jge5lfxtzhx42iff",
    "role": "normal"
  }
}
```
