<h1 id="digitalocean-api-domain-records">Domain Records</h1>

Domain record resources are used to set or retrieve information about the
individual DNS records configured for a domain. This allows you to build
and manage DNS zone files by adding and modifying individual records for a
domain.

The [DigitalOcean DNS management interface](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/networking/dns/)
allows you to configure the following DNS records:

Name  | Description                                                                                                                                        |
------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
A     | This record type is used to map an IPv4 address to a hostname.                                                                                     |
AAAA  | This record type is used to map an IPv6 address to a hostname.                                                                                     |
CAA   | As specified in RFC-6844, this record type can be used to restrict which certificate authorities are permitted to issue certificates for a domain. |
CNAME | This record type defines an alias for your canonical hostname (the one defined by an A or AAAA record).                                            |
MX    | This record type is used to define the mail exchanges used for the domain.                                                                         |
NS    | This record type defines the name servers that are used for this zone.                                                                             |
TXT   | This record type is used to associate a string of text with a hostname, primarily used for verification.                                           |
SRV   | This record type specifies the location (hostname and port number) of servers for specific services.                                               |
SOA   | This record type defines administrative information about the zone. Can only have ttl changed, cannot be deleted                                   |

## List All Domain Records

<a id="opIddomains_list_records"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/domains/example.com/records \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/domains/{domain_name}/records`

To get a listing of all records configured for a domain, send a GET request to `/v2/domains/$DOMAIN_NAME/records`.
The list of records returned can be filtered by using the `name` and `type` query parameters. For example, to only include A records for a domain, send a GET request to `/v2/domains/$DOMAIN_NAME/records?type=A`. `name` must be a fully qualified record name. For example, to only include records matching `sub.example.com`, send a GET request to `/v2/domains/$DOMAIN_NAME/records?name=sub.example.com`. Both name and type may be used together.



<h3 id="list-all-domain-records-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|domain_name|path|string|true|The name of the domain itself.|
|name|query|string|false|A fully qualified record name. For example, to only include records matching sub.example.com, send a GET request to `/v2/domains/$DOMAIN_NAME/records?name=sub.example.com`.|
|type|query|string|false|The type of the DNS record. For example: A, CNAME, TXT, ...|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|A|
|type|AAAA|
|type|CAA|
|type|CNAME|
|type|MX|
|type|NS|
|type|SOA|
|type|SRV|
|type|TXT|

## Create a New Domain Record

<a id="opIddomains_create_record"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/domains/example.com/records \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "data": "162.10.66.0",
    "flags": null,
    "name": "www",
    "port": null,
    "priority": null,
    "tag": null,
    "ttl": 1800,
    "type": "A",
    "weight": null
  }'
```

`POST /v2/domains/{domain_name}/records`

To create a new record to a domain, send a POST request to
`/v2/domains/$DOMAIN_NAME/records`.

The request must include all of the required fields for the domain record type
being added.

See the [attribute table](#tag/Domain-Records) for details regarding record
types and their respective required attributes.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "data": "162.10.66.0",
  "flags": null,
  "name": "www",
  "port": null,
  "priority": null,
  "tag": null,
  "ttl": 1800,
  "type": "A",
  "weight": null
}
```

|domain_name|path|string|true|The name of the domain itself.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» data|body|string|true|Variable data depending on record type. For example, the "data" value for an A record would be the IPv4 address to which the domain will be mapped. For a CAA record, it would contain the domain name of the CA being granted permission to issue certificates.|
|» flags|body|integer \| null|false|An unsigned integer between 0-255 used for CAA records.|
|» name|body|string|true|The host name, alias, or service being defined by the record.|
|» port|body|integer \| null|false|The port for SRV records.|
|» priority|body|integer \| null|false|The priority for SRV and MX records.|

## Update a Domain Record

<a id="opIddomains_update_record"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/domains/example.com/records/3352896 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "blog",
    "type": "CNAME"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/domains/{domain_name}/records/{domain_record_id}`

To update an existing record, send a PUT request to
`/v2/domains/$DOMAIN_NAME/records/$DOMAIN_RECORD_ID`. Any attribute valid for
the record type can be set to a new value for the record.

See the [attribute table](#tag/Domain-Records) for details regarding record
types and their respective attributes.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "blog",
  "type": "CNAME"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-domain-record-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|domain_name|path|string|true|The name of the domain itself.|
|domain_record_id|path|integer|true|The unique identifier of the domain record.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» data|body|string|false|Variable data depending on record type. For example, the "data" value for an A record would be the IPv4 address to which the domain will be mapped. For a CAA record, it would contain the domain name of the CA being granted permission to issue certificates.|
|» flags|body|integer \| null|false|An unsigned integer between 0-255 used for CAA records.|
|» name|body|string|false|The host name, alias, or service being defined by the record.|
|» port|body|integer \| null|false|The port for SRV records.|
|» priority|body|integer \| null|false|The priority for SRV and MX records.|
|» tag|body|string \| null|false|The parameter tag for CAA records. Valid values are "issue", "issuewild", or "iodef"|
|» ttl|body|integer|false|This value is the time to live for the record, in seconds. This defines the time frame that clients can cache queried information before a refresh should be requested.|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of the DNS record. For example: A, CNAME, TXT, ...|
|» weight|body|integer \| null|false|The weight for SRV records.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "domain_record": {
    "data": "162.10.66.0",
    "flags": null,
    "id": 3352896,
    "name": "blog",
    "port": null,
    "priority": null,
    "tag": null,
    "ttl": 1800,
    "type": "A",
    "weight": null
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-domains">Domains</h1>

Domain resources are domain names that you have purchased from a domain
name registrar that you are managing through the
[DigitalOcean DNS interface](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/networking/dns/).

This resource establishes top-level control over each domain. Actions that
affect individual domain records should be taken on the
[Domain Records](#tag/Domain-Records) resource.

## List All Domains

<a id="opIddomains_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/domains \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/domains`

To retrieve a list of all of the domains in your account, send a GET request to `/v2/domains`.

<h3 id="list-all-domains-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "domains": [
    {
      "name": "example.com",
      "ttl": 1800,
      "zone_file": "$ORIGIN example.com.\n$TTL 1800\nexample.com. IN SOA ns1.digitalocean.com. hostmaster.example.com. 1415982609 10800 3600 604800 1800\nexample.com. 1800 IN NS ns1.digitalocean.com.\nexample.com. 1800 IN NS ns2.digitalocean.com.\nexample.com. 1800 IN NS ns3.digitalocean.com.\nexample.com. 1800 IN A 1.2.3.4\n"
    }
  ],
  "links": {},
  "meta": {
    "total": 1
  }
}
```

```json

  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

```json

  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json

  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json

  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

|500|Internal Server Error|Server error.|Inline|

## Create a New Domain

<a id="opIddomains_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/domains \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "example.com"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/domains`

To create a new domain, send a POST request to `/v2/domains`. Set the "name"
attribute to the domain name you are adding. Optionally, you may set the
"ip_address" attribute, and an A record will be automatically created pointing
to the apex domain.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "example.com"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-domain-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» ip_address|body|string|false|This optional attribute may contain an IP address. When provided, an A record will be automatically created pointing to the apex domain.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the domain itself. This should follow the standard domain format of domain.TLD. For instance, `example.com` is a valid domain name.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "domain": {
    "name": "example.com",
    "ttl": 1800,
    "zone_file": null
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-domain-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The response will be a JSON object with a key called `domain`. The value of this will be an object that contains the standard attributes associated with a domain.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|API Rate limit exceeded|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error.|Inline|
|default|Default|Unexpected error|Inline|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-droplet-actions">Droplet Actions</h1>

Droplet actions are tasks that can be executed on a Droplet. These can be
things like rebooting, resizing, snapshotting, etc.

Droplet action requests are generally targeted at one of the "actions"
endpoints for a specific Droplet. The specific actions are usually
initiated by sending a POST request with the action and arguments as
parameters.

Droplet action requests create a Droplet actions object, which can be used
to get information about the status of an action. Creating a Droplet
action is asynchronous: the HTTP call will return the action object before
the action has finished processing on the Droplet. The current status of
an action can be retrieved from either the Droplet actions endpoint or the
global actions endpoint. If a Droplet action is uncompleted it may block
the creation of a subsequent action for that Droplet, the locked attribute
of the Droplet will be true and attempts to create a Droplet action will
fail with a status of 422.

## Acting on Tagged Droplets

<a id="opIddropletActions_post_byTag"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/droplets/actions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "reboot"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/droplets/actions`

Some actions can be performed in bulk on tagged Droplets. The actions can be
initiated by sending a POST to `/v2/droplets/actions?tag_name=$TAG_NAME` with
the action arguments.

Only a sub-set of action types are supported:

- `power_cycle`
- `power_on`
- `power_off`
- `shutdown`
- `enable_ipv6`
- `enable_backups`
- `disable_backups`
- `snapshot`


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "reboot"
}
```

<h3 id="acting-on-tagged-droplets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tag_name|query|string|false|Used to filter Droplets by a specific tag. Can not be combined with `name`.|
|body|body|object|false|The `type` attribute set in the request body will specify the  action that<br>will be taken on the Droplet. Some actions will require additional<br>attributes to be set as well.<br>|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|Specifies the action that will be taken on the Droplet.|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of action to initiate for the Droplet.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of action to initiate for the Droplet.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name to give the new snapshot of the Droplet.|

|» type|disable_backups|

## List Actions for a Droplet

<a id="opIddropletActions_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/droplets/3164444/actions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}/actions`

To retrieve a list of all actions that have been executed for a Droplet, send
a GET request to `/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID/actions`.

The results will be returned as a JSON object with an `actions` key. This will
be set to an array filled with `action` objects containing the standard
`action` attributes.

|droplet_id|path|integer|true|A unique identifier for a Droplet instance.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

## Initiate a Droplet Action

<a id="opIddropletActions_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/droplets/3164444/actions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "reboot"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}/actions`

To initiate an action on a Droplet send a POST request to
`/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID/actions`. In the JSON body to the request,
set the `type` attribute to on of the supported action types:

| Action                                   | Details |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| <nobr>`enable_backups`</nobr>            | Enables backups for a Droplet |
| <nobr>`disable_backups`</nobr>           | Disables backups for a Droplet |
| <nobr>`reboot`</nobr>                    | Reboots a Droplet. A `reboot` action is an attempt to reboot the Droplet in a graceful way, similar to using the `reboot` command from the console. |
| <nobr>`power_cycle`</nobr>               | Power cycles a Droplet. A `powercycle` action is similar to pushing the reset button on a physical machine, it's similar to booting from scratch. |
| <nobr>`shutdown`</nobr>                  | Shutsdown a Droplet. A shutdown action is an attempt to shutdown the Droplet in a graceful way, similar to using the `shutdown` command from the console. Since a `shutdown` command can fail, this action guarantees that the command is issued, not that it succeeds. The preferred way to turn off a Droplet is to attempt a shutdown, with a reasonable timeout, followed by a `power_off` action to ensure the Droplet is off. |
| <nobr>`power_off`</nobr>                 | Powers off a Droplet. A `power_off` event is a hard shutdown and should only be used if the `shutdown` action is not successful. It is similar to cutting the power on a server and could lead to complications. |
| <nobr>`power_on`</nobr>                  | Powers on a Droplet. |
| <nobr>`restore`</nobr>                   | Restore a Droplet using a backup image. The image ID that is passed in must be a backup of the current Droplet instance. The operation will leave any embedded SSH keys intact. |
| <nobr>`password_reset`</nobr>            | Resets the root password for a Droplet. A new password will be provided via email. It must be changed after first use. |
| <nobr>`resize`</nobr>                    | Resizes a Droplet. Set the `size` attribute to a size slug. If a permanent resize with disk changes included is desired, set the `disk` attribute to `true`. |
| <nobr>`rebuild`</nobr>                   | Rebuilds a Droplet from a new base image. Set the `image` attribute to an image ID or slug. |
| <nobr>`rename`</nobr>                    | Renames a Droplet. |
| <nobr>`change_kernel`</nobr>             | Changes a Droplet's kernel. Only applies to Droplets with externally managed kernels. All Droplets created after March 2017 use internal kernels by default. |
| <nobr>`enable_ipv6`</nobr>               | Enables IPv6 for a Droplet. |
| <nobr>`snapshot`</nobr>                  | Takes a snapshot of a Droplet. |


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "reboot"
}
```

<h3 id="initiate-a-droplet-action-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|droplet_id|path|integer|true|A unique identifier for a Droplet instance.|
|body|body|object|false|The `type` attribute set in the request body will specify the  action that<br>will be taken on the Droplet. Some actions will require additional<br>attributes to be set as well.<br>|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|Specifies the action that will be taken on the Droplet.|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of action to initiate for the Droplet.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of action to initiate for the Droplet.|
|» image|body|integer|false|The ID of a backup of the current Droplet instance to restore from.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of action to initiate for the Droplet.|
|» disk|body|boolean|false|When `true`, the Droplet's disk will be resized in addition to its RAM and CPU. This is a permanent change and cannot be reversed as a Droplet's disk size cannot be decreased.|
|» size|body|string|false|The slug identifier for the size to which you wish to resize the Droplet.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of action to initiate for the Droplet.|
|» image|body|string \| integer|false|The image ID of a public or private image or the slug identifier for a public image. The Droplet will be rebuilt using this image as its base.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of action to initiate for the Droplet.|
|» name|body|string|false|The new name for the Droplet.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of action to initiate for the Droplet.|
|» kernel|body|integer|false|A unique number used to identify and reference a specific kernel.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of action to initiate for the Droplet.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name to give the new snapshot of the Droplet.|

## Retrieve a Droplet Action

<a id="opIddropletActions_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/droplets/3164444/actions/36804636 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}/actions/{action_id}`

To retrieve a Droplet action, send a GET request to
`/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID/actions/$ACTION_ID`.

The response will be a JSON object with a key called `action`. The value will
be a Droplet action object.


<h3 id="retrieve-a-droplet-action-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|droplet_id|path|integer|true|A unique identifier for a Droplet instance.|
|action_id|path|integer|true|A unique numeric ID that can be used to identify and reference an action.|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|» id|integer|false|none|A unique numeric ID that can be used to identify and reference an action.|
|» region|object|false|none|none|

|» » slug|string|true|none|A human-readable string that is used as a unique identifier for each region.|
|» region_slug|object|false|none|none|
|» resource_id|integer \| null|false|none|A unique identifier for the resource that the action is associated with.|
|» resource_type|string|false|none|The type of resource that the action is associated with.|
|» started_at|string(date-time)|false|none|A time value given in ISO8601 combined date and time format that represents when the action was initiated.|
|» status|string|false|none|The current status of the action. This can be "in-progress", "completed", or "errored".|
|» type|string|false|none|This is the type of action that the object represents. For example, this could be "transfer" to represent the state of an image transfer action.|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-droplets">Droplets</h1>

A [Droplet](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/droplets/) is a DigitalOcean
virtual machine. By sending requests to the Droplet endpoint, you can
list, create, or delete Droplets.

Some of the attributes will have an object value. The `region` and `image`
objects will all contain the standard attributes of their associated
types. Find more information about each of these objects in their
respective sections.

## List All Droplets

<a id="opIddroplets_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/droplets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/droplets`

To list all Droplets in your account, send a GET request to `/v2/droplets`.

The response body will be a JSON object with a key of `droplets`. This will be
set to an array containing objects each representing a Droplet. These will
contain the standard Droplet attributes.

### Filtering Results by Tag

It's possible to request filtered results by including certain query parameters.
To only list Droplets assigned to a specific tag, include the `tag_name` query
parameter set to the name of the tag in your GET request. For example,
`/v2/droplets?tag_name=$TAG_NAME`.


<h3 id="list-all-droplets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|
|tag_name|query|string|false|Used to filter Droplets by a specific tag. Can not be combined with `name`.|
|name|query|string|false|Used to filter list response by Droplet name returning only exact matches. It is case-insensitive and can not be combined with `tag_name`.|

## Create a New Droplet

<a id="opIddroplets_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/droplets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "backups": true,
    "image": "ubuntu-20-04-x64",
    "ipv6": true,
    "monitoring": true,
    "names": [
      "sub-01.example.com",
      "sub-02.example.com"
    ],
    "region": "nyc3",
    "size": "s-1vcpu-1gb",
    "ssh_keys": [
      289794,
      "3b:16:e4:bf:8b:00:8b:b8:59:8c:a9:d3:f0:19:fa:45"
    ],
    "tags": [
      "env:prod",
      "web"
    ],
    "user_data": "#cloud-config\nruncmd:\n  - touch /test.txt\n",
    "vpc_uuid": "760e09ef-dc84-11e8-981e-3cfdfeaae000"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/droplets`

To create a new Droplet, send a POST request to `/v2/droplets` setting the
required attributes.

A Droplet will be created using the provided information. The response body
will contain a JSON object with a key called `droplet`. The value will be an
object containing the standard attributes for your new Droplet. The response
code, 202 Accepted, does not indicate the success or failure of the operation,
just that the request has been accepted for processing. The `actions` returned
as part of the response's `links` object can be used to check the status
of the Droplet create event.

### Create Multiple Droplets

Creating multiple Droplets is very similar to creating a single Droplet.
Instead of sending `name` as a string, send `names` as an array of strings. A
Droplet will be created for each name you send using the associated
information. Up to ten Droplets may be created this way at a time.

Rather than returning a single Droplet, the response body will contain a JSON
array with a key called `droplets`. This will be set to an array of JSON
objects, each of which will contain the standard Droplet attributes. The
response code, 202 Accepted, does not indicate the success or failure of any
operation, just that the request has been accepted for processing. The array
of `actions` returned as part of the response's `links` object can be used to
check the status of each individual Droplet create event.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "backups": true,
  "image": "ubuntu-20-04-x64",
  "ipv6": true,
  "monitoring": true,
  "names": [
    "sub-01.example.com",
    "sub-02.example.com"
  ],
  "region": "nyc3",
  "size": "s-1vcpu-1gb",
  "ssh_keys": [
    289794,
    "3b:16:e4:bf:8b:00:8b:b8:59:8c:a9:d3:f0:19:fa:45"
  ],
  "tags": [
    "env:prod",
    "web"
  ],
  "user_data": "#cloud-config\nruncmd:\n  - touch /test.txt\n",
  "vpc_uuid": "760e09ef-dc84-11e8-981e-3cfdfeaae000"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-droplet-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The human-readable string you wish to use when displaying the Droplet name. The name, if set to a domain name managed in the DigitalOcean DNS management system, will configure a PTR record for the Droplet. The name set during creation will also determine the hostname for the Droplet in its internal configuration.|
|» backups|body|boolean|false|A boolean indicating whether automated backups should be enabled for the Droplet.|
|» image|body|string \| integer|true|The image ID of a public or private image or the slug identifier for a public image. This image will be the base image for your Droplet.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» ipv6|body|boolean|false|A boolean indicating whether to enable IPv6 on the Droplet.|
|» monitoring|body|boolean|false|A boolean indicating whether to install the DigitalOcean agent for monitoring.|
|» private_networking|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** This parameter has been deprecated. Use `vpc_uuid` instead to specify a VPC network for the Droplet. If no `vpc_uuid` is provided, the Droplet will be placed in your account's default VPC for the region.|
|» region|body|string|false|The slug identifier for the region that you wish to deploy the Droplet in. If the specific datacenter is not not important, a slug prefix (e.g. `nyc`) can be used to deploy the Droplet in any of the that region's locations (`nyc1`, `nyc2`, or `nyc3`). If the region is omitted from the create request completely, the Droplet may deploy in any region.|
|» size|body|string|true|The slug identifier for the size that you wish to select for this Droplet.|
|» ssh_keys|body|[string \| integer]|false|An array containing the IDs or fingerprints of the SSH keys that you wish to embed in the Droplet's root account upon creation.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|A flat array of tag names as strings to apply to the Droplet after it is created. Tag names can either be existing or new tags.|
|» user_data|body|string|false|A string containing 'user data' which may be used to configure the Droplet on first boot, often a 'cloud-config' file or Bash script. It must be plain text and may not exceed 64 KiB in size.|
|» volumes|body|[string]|false|An array of IDs for block storage volumes that will be attached to the Droplet once created. The volumes must not already be attached to an existing Droplet.|
|» vpc_uuid|body|string|false|A string specifying the UUID of the VPC to which the Droplet will be assigned. If excluded, the Droplet will be assigned to your account's default VPC for the region.|
|» with_droplet_agent|body|boolean|false|A boolean indicating whether to install the DigitalOcean agent used for providing access to the Droplet web console in the control panel. By default, the agent is installed on new Droplets but installation errors (i.e. OS not supported) are ignored. To prevent it from being installed, set to `false`. To make installation errors fatal, explicitly set it to `true`.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» names|body|[string]|true|An array of human human-readable strings you wish to use when displaying the Droplet name. Each name, if set to a domain name managed in the DigitalOcean DNS management system, will configure a PTR record for the Droplet. Each name set during creation will also determine the hostname for the Droplet in its internal configuration.|
|» backups|body|boolean|false|A boolean indicating whether automated backups should be enabled for the Droplet.|
|» image|body|string \| integer|true|The image ID of a public or private image or the slug identifier for a public image. This image will be the base image for your Droplet.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» ipv6|body|boolean|false|A boolean indicating whether to enable IPv6 on the Droplet.|
|» monitoring|body|boolean|false|A boolean indicating whether to install the DigitalOcean agent for monitoring.|
|» private_networking|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** This parameter has been deprecated. Use `vpc_uuid` instead to specify a VPC network for the Droplet. If no `vpc_uuid` is provided, the Droplet will be placed in your account's default VPC for the region.|
|» region|body|string|false|The slug identifier for the region that you wish to deploy the Droplet in. If the specific datacenter is not not important, a slug prefix (e.g. `nyc`) can be used to deploy the Droplet in any of the that region's locations (`nyc1`, `nyc2`, or `nyc3`). If the region is omitted from the create request completely, the Droplet may deploy in any region.|
|» size|body|string|true|The slug identifier for the size that you wish to select for this Droplet.|
|» ssh_keys|body|[string \| integer]|false|An array containing the IDs or fingerprints of the SSH keys that you wish to embed in the Droplet's root account upon creation.|
|» » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » *anyOf*|body|integer|false|none|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|A flat array of tag names as strings to apply to the Droplet after it is created. Tag names can either be existing or new tags.|
|» user_data|body|string|false|A string containing 'user data' which may be used to configure the Droplet on first boot, often a 'cloud-config' file or Bash script. It must be plain text and may not exceed 64 KiB in size.|
|» volumes|body|[string]|false|An array of IDs for block storage volumes that will be attached to the Droplet once created. The volumes must not already be attached to an existing Droplet.|
|» vpc_uuid|body|string|false|A string specifying the UUID of the VPC to which the Droplet will be assigned. If excluded, the Droplet will be assigned to your account's default VPC for the region.|
|» with_droplet_agent|body|boolean|false|A boolean indicating whether to install the DigitalOcean agent used for providing access to the Droplet web console in the control panel. By default, the agent is installed on new Droplets but installation errors (i.e. OS not supported) are ignored. To prevent it from being installed, set to `false`. To make installation errors fatal, explicitly set it to `true`.|

<h3 id="create-a-new-droplet-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Accepted|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|API Rate limit exceeded|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error.|Inline|
|default|Default|Unexpected error|Inline|

<h3 id="create-a-new-droplet-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **202**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|droplet|object|true|none|none|
|» backup_ids|[integer]|true|none|An array of backup IDs of any backups that have been taken of the Droplet instance.  Droplet backups are enabled at the time of the instance creation.|
|» created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|A time value given in ISO8601 combined date and time format that represents when the Droplet was created.|
|» disk|integer|true|none|The size of the Droplet's disk in gigabytes.|
|» features|[string]|true|none|An array of features enabled on this Droplet.|
|» id|integer|true|none|A unique identifier for each Droplet instance. This is automatically generated upon Droplet creation.|
|» image|object|true|none|none|
|» » created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|A time value given in ISO8601 combined date and time format that represents when the image was created.|
|» » description|string|false|none|An optional free-form text field to describe an image.|
|» » distribution|string|false|none|The name of a custom image's distribution. Currently, the valid values are  `Arch Linux`, `CentOS`, `CoreOS`, `Debian`, `Fedora`, `Fedora Atomic`,  `FreeBSD`, `Gentoo`, `openSUSE`, `RancherOS`, `Rocky Linux`, `Ubuntu`, and `Unknown`.  Any other value will be accepted but ignored, and `Unknown` will be used in its place.|
|» » error_message|string|false|none|A string containing information about errors that may occur when importing<br> a custom image.|
|» » id|integer|false|read-only|A unique number that can be used to identify and reference a specific image.|
|» » min_disk_size|integer \| null|false|none|The minimum disk size in GB required for a Droplet to use this image.|
|» » name|string|false|none|The display name that has been given to an image.  This is what is shown in the control panel and is generally a descriptive title for the image in question.|
|» » public|boolean|false|none|This is a boolean value that indicates whether the image in question is public or not. An image that is public is available to all accounts. A non-public image is only accessible from your account.|
|» » regions|[string]|false|none|This attribute is an array of the regions that the image is available in. The regions are represented by their identifying slug values.|
|» » size_gigabytes|number(float) \| null|false|none|The size of the image in gigabytes.|
|» » slug|string \| null|false|none|A uniquely identifying string that is associated with each of the DigitalOcean-provided public images. These can be used to reference a public image as an alternative to the numeric id.|
|» » status|string|false|none|A status string indicating the state of a custom image. This may be `NEW`,<br> `available`, `pending`, `deleted`, or `retired`.|

This will initially be set to<br>the kernel of the base image when the Droplet is created.<br>|

## Deleting Droplets by Tag

<a id="opIddroplets_destroy_byTag"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/v2/droplets?tag_name=env%3Atest' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/droplets`

To delete **all** Droplets assigned to a specific tag, include the `tag_name`
query parameter set to the name of the tag in your DELETE request. For
example,  `/v2/droplets?tag_name=$TAG_NAME`.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully.


<h3 id="deleting-droplets-by-tag-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tag_name|query|string|true|Specifies Droplets to be deleted by tag.|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

```json

  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

## Retrieve an Existing Droplet

<a id="opIddroplets_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/droplets/3164444 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

<h3 id="retrieve-an-existing-droplet-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|droplet|object|false|none|none|
|» backup_ids|[integer]|true|none|An array of backup IDs of any backups that have been taken of the Droplet instance.  Droplet backups are enabled at the time of the instance creation.|
|» created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|A time value given in ISO8601 combined date and time format that represents when the Droplet was created.|
|» disk|integer|true|none|The size of the Droplet's disk in gigabytes.|
|» features|[string]|true|none|An array of features enabled on this Droplet.|
|» id|integer|true|none|A unique identifier for each Droplet instance. This is automatically generated upon Droplet creation.|
|» image|object|true|none|none|
|» » created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|A time value given in ISO8601 combined date and time format that represents when the image was created.|
|» » description|string|false|none|An optional free-form text field to describe an image.|
|» » distribution|string|false|none|The name of a custom image's distribution. Currently, the valid values are  `Arch Linux`, `CentOS`, `CoreOS`, `Debian`, `Fedora`, `Fedora Atomic`,  `FreeBSD`, `Gentoo`, `openSUSE`, `RancherOS`, `Rocky Linux`, `Ubuntu`, and `Unknown`.  Any other value will be accepted but ignored, and `Unknown` will be used in its place.|
|» » error_message|string|false|none|A string containing information about errors that may occur when importing<br> a custom image.|
|» » id|integer|false|read-only|A unique number that can be used to identify and reference a specific image.|
|» » min_disk_size|integer \| null|false|none|The minimum disk size in GB required for a Droplet to use this image.|
|» » name|string|false|none|The display name that has been given to an image.  This is what is shown in the control panel and is generally a descriptive title for the image in question.|
|» » public|boolean|false|none|This is a boolean value that indicates whether the image in question is public or not. An image that is public is available to all accounts. A non-public image is only accessible from your account.|
|» » regions|[string]|false|none|This attribute is an array of the regions that the image is available in. The regions are represented by their identifying slug values.|
|» » size_gigabytes|number(float) \| null|false|none|The size of the image in gigabytes.|
|» » slug|string \| null|false|none|A uniquely identifying string that is associated with each of the DigitalOcean-provided public images. These can be used to reference a public image as an alternative to the numeric id.|
|» » status|string|false|none|A status string indicating the state of a custom image. This may be `NEW`,<br> `available`, `pending`, `deleted`, or `retired`.|

## Delete an Existing Droplet

<a id="opIddroplets_destroy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/droplets/3164444 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}`

To delete a Droplet, send a DELETE request to `/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID`.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully.


<h3 id="delete-an-existing-droplet-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|droplet_id|path|integer|true|A unique identifier for a Droplet instance.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## List Backups for a Droplet

<a id="opIddroplets_list_backups"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/droplets/3164444/backups \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}/backups`

To retrieve any backups associated with a Droplet, send a GET request to
`/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID/backups`.

You will get back a JSON object that has a `backups` key. This will be set to
an array of backup objects, each of which contain the standard
Droplet backup attributes.


<h3 id="list-backups-for-a-droplet-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|droplet_id|path|integer|true|A unique identifier for a Droplet instance.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "backups": [
    {
      "created_at": "2020-07-29T01:44:35Z",
      "distribution": "Ubuntu",
      "id": 67539192,
      "min_disk_size": 50,
      "name": "web-01- 2020-07-29",
      "public": false,
      "regions": [
        "nyc3"
      ],
      "size_gigabytes": 2.34,
      "slug": null,
      "type": "backup"
    }
  ],
  "links": {},
  "meta": {
    "total": 1
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h3 id="list-backups-for-a-droplet-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|

|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|Inline|
|404|Not Found|The resource was not found.|Inline|

|500|Internal Server Error|Server error.|Inline|

## List Associated Resources for a Droplet

<a id="opIddroplets_list_associatedResources"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/droplets/3164444/destroy_with_associated_resources \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}/destroy_with_associated_resources`

To list the associated billable resources that can be destroyed along with a
Droplet, send a GET request to the
`/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID/destroy_with_associated_resources` endpoint.

The response will be a JSON object containing `snapshots`, `volumes`, and
`volume_snapshots` keys. Each will be set to an array of objects containing
information about the associated resources.


<h3 id="list-associated-resources-for-a-droplet-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|droplet_id|path|integer|true|A unique identifier for a Droplet instance.|

## Destroy a Droplet and All of its Associated Resources (Dangerous)

<a id="opIddroplets_destroy_withAssociatedResourcesDangerous"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/droplets/3164444/destroy_with_associated_resources/dangerous \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'X-Dangerous: true'
```

`DELETE /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}/destroy_with_associated_resources/dangerous`

To destroy a Droplet along with all of its associated resources, send a DELETE
request to the `/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID/destroy_with_associated_resources/dangerous`
endpoint. The headers of this request must include an `X-Dangerous` key set to
`true`. To preview which resources will be destroyed, first query the
Droplet's associated resources. This operation _can not_ be reverse and should
be used with caution.

A successful response will include a 202 response code and no content. Use the
status endpoint to check on the success or failure of the destruction of the
individual resources.


<h3 id="destroy-a-droplet-and-all-of-its-associated-resources-dangerous-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|droplet_id|path|integer|true|A unique identifier for a Droplet instance.|
|X-Dangerous|header|boolean|true|Acknowledge this action will destroy the Droplet and all associated resources and _can not_ be reversed.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Retry a Droplet Destroy with Associated Resources Request

<a id="opIddroplets_destroy_retryWithAssociatedResources"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/droplets/3164444/destroy_with_associated_resources/retry \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}/destroy_with_associated_resources/retry`

If the status of a request to destroy a Droplet with its associated resources
reported any errors, it can be retried by sending a POST request to the
`/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID/destroy_with_associated_resources/retry` endpoint.

Only one destroy can be active at a time per Droplet. If a retry is issued
while another destroy is in progress for the Droplet a 409 status code will
be returned. A successful response will include a 202 response code and no
content.


<h3 id="retry-a-droplet-destroy-with-associated-resources-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|droplet_id|path|integer|true|A unique identifier for a Droplet instance.|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 409 Response

```json

  "id": "conflict",
  "message": "The request could not be completed due to a conflict."
}
```


## Selectively Destroy a Droplet and its Associated Resources

<a id="opIddroplets_destroy_withAssociatedResourcesSelective"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/droplets/3164444/destroy_with_associated_resources/selective \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "floating_ips": [
      "6186916"
    ],
    "reserved_ips": [
      "6186916"
    ],
    "snapshots": [
      "61486916"
    ],
    "volume_snapshots": [
      "edb0478d-7436-11ea-86e6-0a58ac144b91"
    ],
    "volumes": [
      "ba49449a-7435-11ea-b89e-0a58ac14480f"
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}/destroy_with_associated_resources/selective`

To destroy a Droplet along with a sub-set of its associated resources, send a
DELETE request to the `/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID/destroy_with_associated_resources/selective`
endpoint. The JSON body of the request should include `reserved_ips`, `snapshots`, `volumes`,
or `volume_snapshots` keys each set to an array of IDs for the associated
resources to be destroyed. The IDs can be found by querying the Droplet's
associated resources. Any associated resource not included in the request
will remain and continue to accrue changes on your account.

A successful response will include a 202 response code and no content. Use
the status endpoint to check on the success or failure of the destruction of
the individual resources.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "floating_ips": [
    "6186916"
  ],
  "reserved_ips": [
    "6186916"
  ],
  "snapshots": [
    "61486916"
  ],
  "volume_snapshots": [
    "edb0478d-7436-11ea-86e6-0a58ac144b91"
  ],
  "volumes": [
    "ba49449a-7435-11ea-b89e-0a58ac14480f"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="selectively-destroy-a-droplet-and-its-associated-resources-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|droplet_id|path|integer|true|A unique identifier for a Droplet instance.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» floating_ips|body|[string]|false|**Deprecated.** An array of unique identifiers for the floating IPs to be scheduled for deletion.|
|» reserved_ips|body|[string]|false|An array of unique identifiers for the reserved IPs to be scheduled for deletion.|
|» snapshots|body|[string]|false|An array of unique identifiers for the snapshots to be scheduled for deletion.|
|» volume_snapshots|body|[string]|false|An array of unique identifiers for the volume snapshots to be scheduled for deletion.|
|» volumes|body|[string]|false|An array of unique identifiers for the volumes to be scheduled for deletion.|

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

## List Neighbors for a Droplet

<a id="opIddroplets_list_neighbors"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/droplets/3164444/neighbors \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}/neighbors`

To retrieve a list of any "neighbors" (i.e. Droplets that are co-located on
the same physical hardware) for a specific Droplet, send a GET request to
`/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID/neighbors`.

The results will be returned as a JSON object with a key of `droplets`. This
will be set to an array containing objects representing any other Droplets
that share the same physical hardware. An empty array indicates that the
Droplet is not co-located any other Droplets associated with your account.


<h3 id="list-neighbors-for-a-droplet-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|droplet_id|path|integer|true|A unique identifier for a Droplet instance.|

## List Snapshots for a Droplet

<a id="opIddroplets_list_snapshots"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/droplets/3164444/snapshots \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/droplets/{droplet_id}/snapshots`

To retrieve the snapshots that have been created from a Droplet, send a GET
request to `/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID/snapshots`.

You will get back a JSON object that has a `snapshots` key. This will be set
to an array of snapshot objects, each of which contain the standard Droplet
snapshot attributes.

|droplet_id|path|integer|true|A unique identifier for a Droplet instance.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

## List All Droplet Neighbors

<a id="opIddroplets_list_neighborsIds"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/reports/droplet_neighbors_ids \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/reports/droplet_neighbors_ids`

To retrieve a list of all Droplets that are co-located on the same physical
hardware, send a GET request to `/v2/reports/droplet_neighbors_ids`.

The results will be returned as a JSON object with a key of `neighbor_ids`.
This will be set to an array of arrays. Each array will contain a set of
Droplet IDs for Droplets that share a physical server. An empty array
indicates that all Droplets associated with your account are located on
separate physical hardware.


> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "neighbor_ids": [
    [
      168671828,
      168663509,
      168671815
    ],
    [
      168671883,
      168671750
    ]
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-firewalls">Firewalls</h1>

[DigitalOcean Cloud Firewalls](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/networking/firewalls/)
provide the ability to restrict network access to and from a Droplet
allowing you to define which ports will accept inbound or outbound
connections. By sending requests to the `/v2/firewalls` endpoint, you can
list, create, or delete firewalls as well as modify access rules.

## List All Firewalls

<a id="opIdfirewalls_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/firewalls \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/firewalls`

To list all of the firewalls available on your account, send a GET request to `/v2/firewalls`.

<h3 id="list-all-firewalls-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

## Create a New Firewall

<a id="opIdfirewalls_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/firewalls \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "droplet_ids": [
      8043964
    ],
    "inbound_rules": [
      {
        "ports": "80",
        "protocol": "tcp",
        "sources": {
          "load_balancer_uids": [
            "4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6"
          ]
        }
      },
      {
        "ports": "22",
        "protocol": "tcp",
        "sources": {
          "addresses": [
            "18.0.0.0/8"
          ],
          "tags": [
            "gateway"
          ]
        }
      }
    ],
    "name": "firewall",
    "outbound_rules": [
      {
        "destinations": {
          "addresses": [
            "0.0.0.0/0",
            "::/0"
          ]
        },
        "ports": "80",
        "protocol": "tcp"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/firewalls`

To create a new firewall, send a POST request to `/v2/firewalls`. The request
must contain at least one inbound or outbound access rule.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "droplet_ids": [
    8043964
  ],
  "inbound_rules": [
    {
      "ports": "80",
      "protocol": "tcp",
      "sources": {
        "load_balancer_uids": [
          "4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6"
        ]
      }
    },

      "protocol": "tcp",
      "sources": {
        "addresses": [
          "18.0.0.0/8"
        ],
        "tags": [
          "gateway"
        ]
      }
    }
  ],
  "name": "firewall",
  "outbound_rules": [
    {
      "destinations": {
        "addresses": [
          "0.0.0.0/0",
          "::/0"
        ]
      },
      "ports": "80",
      "protocol": "tcp"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Update a Firewall

<a id="opIdfirewalls_update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/firewalls/bb4b2611-3d72-467b-8602-280330ecd65c \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "droplet_ids": [
      8043964
    ],
    "inbound_rules": [
      {
        "ports": "8080",
        "protocol": "tcp",
        "sources": {
          "load_balancer_uids": [
            "4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6"
          ]
        }
      },
      {
        "ports": "22",
        "protocol": "tcp",
        "sources": {
          "addresses": [
            "18.0.0.0/8"
          ],
          "tags": [
            "gateway"
          ]
        }
      }
    ],
    "name": "frontend-firewall",
    "outbound_rules": [
      {
        "destinations": {
          "addresses": [
            "0.0.0.0/0",
            "::/0"
          ]
        },
        "ports": "8080",
        "protocol": "tcp"
      }
    ],
    "tags": [
      "frontend"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/firewalls/{firewall_id}`

To update the configuration of an existing firewall, send a PUT request to
`/v2/firewalls/$FIREWALL_ID`. The request should contain a full representation
of the firewall including existing attributes. **Note that any attributes that
are not provided will be reset to their default values.**


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "droplet_ids": [
    8043964
  ],
  "inbound_rules": [
    {
      "ports": "8080",
      "protocol": "tcp",
      "sources": {
        "load_balancer_uids": [
          "4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6"
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "ports": "22",
      "protocol": "tcp",
      "sources": {
        "addresses": [
          "18.0.0.0/8"
        ],
        "tags": [
          "gateway"
        ]
      }
    }
  ],
  "name": "frontend-firewall",
  "outbound_rules": [
    {
      "destinations": {
        "addresses": [
          "0.0.0.0/0",
          "::/0"
        ]
      },
      "ports": "8080",
      "protocol": "tcp"
    }
  ],
  "tags": [
    "frontend"
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|

|body|body|object|false|none|
|» droplet_ids|body|[integer]|false|An array containing the IDs of the Droplets assigned to the firewall.|
|» name|body|string|true|A human-readable name for a firewall. The name must begin with an alphanumeric character. Subsequent characters must either be alphanumeric characters, a period (.), or a dash (-).|
|» tags|body|object|false|none|
|» inbound_rules|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » ports|body|string|true|The ports on which traffic will be allowed specified as a string containing a single port, a range (e.g. "8000-9000"), or "0" when all ports are open for a protocol. For ICMP rules this parameter will always return "0".|
|» » protocol|body|string|true|The type of traffic to be allowed. This may be one of `tcp`, `udp`, or `icmp`.|
|» » sources|body|object|true|none|
|» » » addresses|body|[string]|false|An array of strings containing the IPv4 addresses, IPv6 addresses, IPv4 CIDRs, and/or IPv6 CIDRs to which the firewall will allow traffic.|

## Delete a Firewall

<a id="opIdfirewalls_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/firewalls/bb4b2611-3d72-467b-8602-280330ecd65c \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/firewalls/{firewall_id}`

To delete a firewall send a DELETE request to `/v2/firewalls/$FIREWALL_ID`.

```bash
        "protocol": "tcp"
```

`POST /v2/firewalls/{firewall_id}/rules`

To add additional access rules to a firewall, send a POST request to
`/v2/firewalls/$FIREWALL_ID/rules`. The body of the request may include an
inbound_rules and/or outbound_rules attribute containing an array of rules to
be added.

No response body will be sent back, but the response code will indicate
success. Specifically, the response code will be a 204, which means that the
action was successful with no returned body data.

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-floating-ip-actions">Floating IP Actions</h1>

As of 16 June 2022, we have renamed the Floating IP product to [Reserved IPs](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/api-reference/#tag/Reserved-IPs).
The Reserved IP product's endpoints function the exact same way as Floating IPs.
The only difference is the name change throughout the URLs and fields.
For example, the `floating_ips` field is now the `reserved_ips` field.
The Floating IP endpoints will remain active until fall 2023 before being
permanently deprecated.

With the exception of the [Projects API](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/api-reference/#tag/Projects),
we will reflect this change as an additional field in the responses across the API
where the `floating_ip` field is used. For example, the Droplet metadata response
will contain the field `reserved_ips` in addition to the `floating_ips` field.
Floating IPs retrieved using the Projects API will retain the original name.

Floating IP actions are commands that can be given to a DigitalOcean
floating IP. These requests are made on the actions endpoint of a specific
floating IP.

An action object is returned. These objects hold the current status of the
requested action.

## List All Actions for a Floating IP

<a id="opIdfloatingIPsAction_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/floating_ips/45.55.96.47/actions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/floating_ips/{floating_ip}/actions`

To retrieve all actions that have been executed on a floating IP, send a GET request to `/v2/floating_ips/$FLOATING_IP/actions`.

## Initiate a Floating IP Action

<a id="opIdfloatingIPsAction_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/floating_ips/45.55.96.47/actions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "assign"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/floating_ips/{floating_ip}/actions`

To initiate an action on a floating IP send a POST request to
`/v2/floating_ips/$FLOATING_IP/actions`. In the JSON body to the request,
set the `type` attribute to on of the supported action types:

| Action     | Details
|------------|--------
| `assign`   | Assigns a floating IP to a Droplet
| `unassign` | Unassign a floating IP from a Droplet


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "assign"
}
```

<h3 id="initiate-a-floating-ip-action-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|floating_ip|path|string(ipv4)|true|A floating IP address.|
|body|body|object|false|The `type` attribute set in the request body will specify the action that<br>will be taken on the floating IP.<br>|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of action to initiate for the floating IP.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of action to initiate for the floating IP.|
|» droplet_id|body|integer|true|The ID of the Droplet that the floating IP will be assigned to.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|assign|
|» type|unassign|
|» type|assign|
|» type|unassign|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-floating-ips">Floating IPs</h1>

As of 16 June 2022, we have renamed the Floating IP product to [Reserved IPs](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/api-reference/#tag/Reserved-IPs).
The Reserved IP product's endpoints function the exact same way as Floating IPs.
The only difference is the name change throughout the URLs and fields.
For example, the `floating_ips` field is now the `reserved_ips` field.
The Floating IP endpoints will remain active until fall 2023 before being
permanently deprecated.

With the exception of the [Projects API](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/api-reference/#tag/Projects),
we will reflect this change as an additional field in the responses across the API
where the `floating_ip` field is used. For example, the Droplet metadata response
will contain the field `reserved_ips` in addition to the `floating_ips` field.
Floating IPs retrieved using the Projects API will retain the original name.

[DigitalOcean Floating IPs](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/networking/floating-ips/)
are publicly-accessible static IP addresses that can be mapped to one of
your Droplets. They can be used to create highly available setups or other
configurations requiring movable addresses.

Floating IPs are bound to a specific region.

## List All Floating IPs

<a id="opIdfloatingIPs_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/floating_ips \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/floating_ips`

To list all of the floating IPs available on your account, send a GET request to `/v2/floating_ips`.

## Create a New Floating IP

<a id="opIdfloatingIPs_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/floating_ips \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "droplet_id": 2457247
  }'
```

`POST /v2/floating_ips`

On creation, a floating IP must be either assigned to a Droplet or reserved to a region.
* To create a new floating IP assigned to a Droplet, send a POST
  request to `/v2/floating_ips` with the `droplet_id` attribute.

* To create a new floating IP reserved to a region, send a POST request to
  `/v2/floating_ips` with the `region` attribute.

**Note**:  In addition to the standard rate limiting, only 12 floating IPs may be created per 60 seconds.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "droplet_id": 2457247
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-floating-ip-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» droplet_id|body|integer|true|The ID of the Droplet that the floating IP will be assigned to.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» project_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The UUID of the project to which the floating IP will be assigned.|
|» region|body|string|true|The slug identifier for the region the floating IP will be reserved to.|

## Retrieve an Existing Floating IP

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/floating_ips/45.55.96.47 \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

## Delete a Floating IP

<a id="opIdfloatingIPs_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/floating_ips/45.55.96.47 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/floating_ips/{floating_ip}`

To delete a floating IP and remove it from your account, send a DELETE request
to `/v2/floating_ips/$FLOATING_IP_ADDR`.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully.


<h3 id="delete-a-floating-ip-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|floating_ip|path|string(ipv4)|true|A floating IP address.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-functions">Functions</h1>

[Serverless functions](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/functions) are blocks of code that run on demand without the need to manage any infrastructure.
You can develop functions on your local machine and then deploy them to a namespace using `doctl`, the [official DigitalOcean CLI tool](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/doctl).

The Serverless Functions API currently only supports creating and managing namespaces.

## List Namespaces

<a id="opIdfunctions_list_namespaces"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/functions/namespaces \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/functions/namespaces`

Returns a list of namespaces associated with the current user. To get all namespaces, send a GET request to `/v2/functions/namespaces`.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "namespaces": [
    {
      "api_host": "https://api_host.io",
      "created_at": "2022-09-14T04:16:45Z",
      "key": "d1zcd455h01mqjfs4s2eaewyejehi5f2uj4etqq3h7cera8iwkub6xg5of1wdde2",
      "label": "my namespace",
      "namespace": "fn-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx",
      "region": "nyc1",
      "updated_at": "2022-09-14T04:16:45Z",
      "uuid": "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
```

## Create Namespace

<a id="opIdfunctions_create_namespace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/functions/namespaces \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "label": "my namespace",
    "region": "nyc1"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/functions/namespaces`

Creates a new serverless functions namespace in the desired region and associates it with the provided label. A namespace is a collection of functions and their associated packages, triggers, and project specifications. To create a namespace, send a POST request to `/v2/functions/namespaces` with the `region` and `label` properties.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "label": "my namespace",
  "region": "nyc1"
}
```

<h3 id="create-namespace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» label|body|string|true|The namespace's unique name.|
|» region|body|string|true|The [datacenter region](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/platform/availability-matrix/#available-datacenters) in which to create the namespace.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "namespace": {
    "api_host": "https://api_host.io",
    "created_at": "2022-09-14T04:16:45Z",
    "key": "d1zcd455h01mqjfs4s2eaewyejehi5f2uj4etqq3h7cera8iwkub6xg5of1wdde2",
    "label": "my namespace",
    "namespace": "fn-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "region": "nyc1",
    "updated_at": "2022-09-14T04:16:45Z",
    "uuid": "xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx"
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "bad_request",
  "message": "Invalid request payload: missing label field",
  "request_id": "4851a473-1621-42ea-b2f9-5071c0ea8414"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unprocessable_entity",
  "message": "namespace limit reached",
  "request_id": "a3275238-3d04-4405-a123-55c389b406c0"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Get Namespace

<a id="opIdfunctions_get_namespace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/functions/namespaces/fn-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/functions/namespaces/{namespace_id}`

Gets the namespace details for the given namespace UUID. To get namespace details, send a GET request to `/v2/functions/namespaces/$NAMESPACE_ID` with no parameters.

## Delete Namespace

<a id="opIdfunctions_delete_namespace"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/functions/namespaces/fn-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/functions/namespaces/{namespace_id}`

Deletes the given namespace.  When a namespace is deleted all assets, in the namespace are deleted, this includes packages, functions and triggers. Deleting a namespace is a destructive operation and assets in the namespace are not recoverable after deletion. Some metadata is retained, such as activations, or soft deleted for reporting purposes.
To delete namespace, send a DELETE request to `/v2/functions/namespaces/$NAMESPACE_ID`.
A successful deletion returns a 204 response.

<h3 id="delete-namespace-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace_id|path|string|true|The ID of the namespace to be managed.|

> Example responses

```json
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "namespace not found",
  "request_id": "88d17b7a-630b-4083-99ce-5b91045efdb4"
}
```

> 429 Response


> 500 Response

```json
}
```

> default Response

```json
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

`GET /v2/functions/namespaces/{namespace_id}/triggers`

Returns a list of triggers associated with the current user and namespace. To get all triggers, send a GET request to `/v2/functions/namespaces/$NAMESPACE_ID/triggers`.

<h3 id="list-triggers-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|---|---|---|---|---|

```json
}
```

## Create Trigger

<a id="opIdfunctions_create_trigger"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/functions/namespaces/fn-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx/triggers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "function": "hello",
    "is_enabled": true,
    "name": "my trigger",
    "scheduled_details": {
      "body": {
        "name": "Welcome to DO!"
      },
      "cron": "* * * * *"
    },
    "type": "SCHEDULED"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/functions/namespaces/{namespace_id}/triggers`

Creates a new trigger for a given function in a namespace. To create a trigger, send a POST request to `/v2/functions/namespaces/$NAMESPACE_ID/triggers` with the `name`, `function`, `type`, `is_enabled` and `scheduled_details` properties.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "function": "hello",
  "is_enabled": true,
  "name": "my trigger",
  "scheduled_details": {
    "body": {
      "name": "Welcome to DO!"
    },
    "cron": "* * * * *"
  },
  "type": "SCHEDULED"
}
```

<h3 id="create-trigger-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace_id|path|string|true|The ID of the namespace to be managed.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» function|body|string|true|Name of function(action) that exists in the given namespace.|
|» is_enabled|body|boolean|true|Indicates weather the trigger is paused or unpaused.|
|» name|body|string|true|The trigger's unique name within the namespace.|
|» scheduled_details|body|object|true|Trigger details for SCHEDULED type, where body is optional.<br>|
|» » body|body|object \| null|false|Optional data to be sent to function while triggering the function.|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » cron|body|string|true|valid cron expression string which is required for SCHEDULED type triggers.|
|» type|body|string|true|One of different type of triggers. Currently only SCHEDULED is supported.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "trigger": {
    "created_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z",
    "function": "hello",
    "is_enabled": true,
    "name": "my trigger",
    "namespace": "fn-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "scheduled_details": {
      "body": {
        "name": "Welcome to DO!"
      },
      "cron": "* * * * *"
    },

      "last_run_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z",
      "next_run_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z"
    },
    "type": "SCHEDULED",
    "updated_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z"
  }
}
```


```json
}
```

## Get Trigger

<a id="opIdfunctions_get_trigger"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/functions/namespaces/fn-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx/triggers/my%20trigger \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/functions/namespaces/{namespace_id}/triggers/{trigger_name}`

Gets the trigger details. To get the trigger details, send a GET request to `/v2/functions/namespaces/$NAMESPACE_ID/triggers/$TRIGGER_NAME`.

<h3 id="get-trigger-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace_id|path|string|true|The ID of the namespace to be managed.|
|trigger_name|path|string|true|The name of the trigger to be managed.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "trigger": {
    "created_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z",
    "function": "hello",
    "is_enabled": true,
    "name": "my trigger",
    "namespace": "fn-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "scheduled_details": {
      "body": {
        "name": "Welcome to DO!"
      },
      "cron": "* * * * *"
    },
    "scheduled_runs": {
      "last_run_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z",
      "next_run_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z"
    },
    "type": "SCHEDULED",
    "updated_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z"
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "namespace not found",
  "request_id": "88d17b7a-630b-4083-99ce-5b91045efdb4"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```
