## Update Trigger

<a id="opIdfunctions_update_trigger"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/functions/namespaces/fn-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx/triggers/my%20trigger \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "is_enabled": true,
    "scheduled_details": {
      "body": {
        "name": "Welcome to DO!"
      },
      "cron": "* * * * *"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/functions/namespaces/{namespace_id}/triggers/{trigger_name}`

Updates the details of the given trigger. To update a trigger, send a PUT request to `/v2/functions/namespaces/$NAMESPACE_ID/triggers/$TRIGGER_NAME` with new values for the `is_enabled ` or `scheduled_details` properties.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "is_enabled": true,
  "scheduled_details": {
    "body": {
      "name": "Welcome to DO!"
    },
    "cron": "* * * * *"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-trigger-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace_id|path|string|true|The ID of the namespace to be managed.|
|trigger_name|path|string|true|The name of the trigger to be managed.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» is_enabled|body|boolean|false|Indicates weather the trigger is paused or unpaused.|
|» scheduled_details|body|object|false|Trigger details for SCHEDULED type, where body is optional.<br>|
|» » body|body|object \| null|false|Optional data to be sent to function while triggering the function.|
|» » » name|body|string|false|none|
|» » cron|body|string|true|valid cron expression string which is required for SCHEDULED type triggers.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "trigger": {
    "created_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z",
    "function": "hello",
    "is_enabled": true,
    "name": "my trigger",
    "namespace": "fn-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx",
    "scheduled_details": {
      "body": {
        "name": "Welcome to DO!"
      },
      "cron": "* * * * *"
    },
    "scheduled_runs": {
      "last_run_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z",
      "next_run_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z"
    },
    "type": "SCHEDULED",
    "updated_at": "2022-11-11T04:16:45Z"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
  "id": "bad_request",
  "message": "validating create trigger: validation error: missing trigger name, missing function name, missing source details",
  "request_id": "4851a473-1621-42ea-b2f9-5071c0ea8414"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json

  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "namespace not found",
  "request_id": "88d17b7a-630b-4083-99ce-5b91045efdb4"
```

```json
  "id": "too_many_requests",

```

## Delete Trigger

<a id="opIdfunctions_delete_trigger"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/functions/namespaces/fn-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx/triggers/my%20trigger \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/functions/namespaces/{namespace_id}/triggers/{trigger_name}`

Deletes the given trigger.
To delete trigger, send a DELETE request to `/v2/functions/namespaces/$NAMESPACE_ID/triggers/$TRIGGER_NAME`.
A successful deletion returns a 204 response.

|trigger_name|path|string|true|The name of the trigger to be managed.|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-image-actions">Image Actions</h1>

Image actions are commands that can be given to a DigitalOcean image. In
general, these requests are made on the actions endpoint of a specific
image.

An image action object is returned. These objects hold the current status
of the requested action.

## List All Actions for an Image

<a id="opIdimageActions_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/images/62137902/actions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/images/{image_id}/actions`

To retrieve all actions that have been executed on an image, send a GET request to `/v2/images/$IMAGE_ID/actions`.

|image_id|path|integer|true|A unique number that can be used to identify and reference a specific image.|

## Initiate an Image Action

<a id="opIdimageActions_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/images/62137902/actions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "convert"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/images/{image_id}/actions`

The following actions are available on an Image.

## Convert an Image to a Snapshot

To convert an image, for example, a backup to a snapshot, send a POST request
to `/v2/images/$IMAGE_ID/actions`. Set the `type` attribute to `convert`.

## Transfer an Image

To transfer an image to another region, send a POST request to
`/v2/images/$IMAGE_ID/actions`. Set the `type` attribute to `transfer` and set
`region` attribute to the slug identifier of the region you wish to transfer
to.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "convert"
}
```

<h3 id="initiate-an-image-action-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|image_id|path|integer|true|A unique number that can be used to identify and reference a specific image.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The action to be taken on the image. Can be either `convert` or `transfer`.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The action to be taken on the image. Can be either `convert` or `transfer`.|
|» region|body|string|true|The slug identifier for the region where the resource will initially be  available.|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-images">Images</h1>

A DigitalOcean [image](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/images/) can be
used to create a Droplet and may come in a number of flavors. Currently,
there are five types of images: snapshots, backups, applications,
distributions, and custom images.

* [Snapshots](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/images/snapshots/) provide
a full copy of an existing Droplet instance taken on demand.

* [Backups](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/images/backups/) are similar
to snapshots but are created automatically at regular intervals when
enabled for a Droplet.

* [Custom images](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/images/custom-images/)
are Linux-based virtual machine images (raw, qcow2, vhdx, vdi, and vmdk
formats are supported) that you may upload for use on DigitalOcean.

* Distributions are the public Linux distributions that are available to
be used as a base to create Droplets.

* Applications, or [1-Click Apps](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/one-clicks/),
are distributions pre-configured with additional software.

To interact with images, you will generally send requests to the images
endpoint at /v2/images.

## List All Images

<a id="opIdimages_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/images \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/images`

To list all of the images available on your account, send a GET request to /v2/images.

## Filtering Results
-----

It's possible to request filtered results by including certain query parameters.

**Image Type**

Either 1-Click Application or OS Distribution images can be filtered by using the `type` query parameter.

> Important: The `type` query parameter does not directly relate to the `type` attribute.

To retrieve only ***distribution*** images, include the `type` query parameter set to distribution, `/v2/images?type=distribution`.

To retrieve only ***application*** images, include the `type` query parameter set to application, `/v2/images?type=application`.

**User Images**

To retrieve only the private images of a user, include the `private` query parameter set to true, `/v2/images?private=true`.

**Tags**

To list all images assigned to a specific tag, include the `tag_name` query parameter set to the name of the tag in your GET request. For example, `/v2/images?tag_name=$TAG_NAME`.


<h3 id="list-all-images-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|query|string|false|Filters results based on image type which can be either `application` or `distribution`.|
|private|query|boolean|false|Used to filter only user images.|
|tag_name|query|string|false|Used to filter images by a specific tag.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|application|
|type|distribution|

## Create a Custom Image

<a id="opIdimages_create_custom"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/images \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Cloud-optimized image w/ small footprint",
    "distribution": "Ubuntu",
    "name": "ubuntu-18.04-minimal",
    "region": "nyc3",
    "tags": [
      "base-image",
      "prod"
    ],
    "url": "http://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/minimal/releases/bionic/release/ubuntu-18.04-minimal-cloudimg-amd64.img"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/images`

To create a new custom image, send a POST request to /v2/images.
The body must contain a url attribute pointing to a Linux virtual machine
image to be imported into DigitalOcean.
The image must be in the raw, qcow2, vhdx, vdi, or vmdk format.
It may be compressed using gzip or bzip2 and must be smaller than 100 GB after
 being decompressed.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Cloud-optimized image w/ small footprint",
  "distribution": "Ubuntu",
  "name": "ubuntu-18.04-minimal",
  "region": "nyc3",
  "tags": [
    "base-image",
    "prod"
  ],
  "url": "http://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/minimal/releases/bionic/release/ubuntu-18.04-minimal-cloudimg-amd64.img"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-custom-image-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|An optional free-form text field to describe an image.|
|» distribution|body|string|false|The name of a custom image's distribution. Currently, the valid values are  `Arch Linux`, `CentOS`, `CoreOS`, `Debian`, `Fedora`, `Fedora Atomic`,  `FreeBSD`, `Gentoo`, `openSUSE`, `RancherOS`, `Rocky Linux`, `Ubuntu`, and `Unknown`.  Any other value will be accepted but ignored, and `Unknown` will be used in its place.|
|» name|body|string|true|The display name that has been given to an image.  This is what is shown in the control panel and is generally a descriptive title for the image in question.|
|» region|body|string|true|The slug identifier for the region where the resource will initially be  available.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|A flat array of tag names as strings to be applied to the resource. Tag names may be for either existing or new tags.|
|» url|body|string|true|A URL from which the custom Linux virtual machine image may be retrieved.  The image it points to must be in the raw, qcow2, vhdx, vdi, or vmdk format.  It may be compressed using gzip or bzip2 and must be smaller than 100 GB after being decompressed.|

## Update an Image

<a id="opIdimages_update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/images/62137902 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": " ",
    "distribution": "Ubuntu",
    "name": "Nifty New Snapshot"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/images/{image_id}`

To update an image, send a `PUT` request to `/v2/images/$IMAGE_ID`.
Set the `name` attribute to the new value you would like to use.
For custom images, the `description` and `distribution` attributes may also be updated.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": " ",
  "distribution": "Ubuntu",
  "name": "Nifty New Snapshot"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-image-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|image_id|path|integer|true|A unique number that can be used to identify and reference a specific image.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|An optional free-form text field to describe an image.|
|» distribution|body|string|false|The name of a custom image's distribution. Currently, the valid values are  `Arch Linux`, `CentOS`, `CoreOS`, `Debian`, `Fedora`, `Fedora Atomic`,  `FreeBSD`, `Gentoo`, `openSUSE`, `RancherOS`, `Rocky Linux`, `Ubuntu`, and `Unknown`.  Any other value will be accepted but ignored, and `Unknown` will be used in its place.|
|» name|body|string|false|The display name that has been given to an image.  This is what is shown in the control panel and is generally a descriptive title for the image in question.|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-kubernetes">Kubernetes</h1>

[DigitalOcean Kubernetes](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/kubernetes/)
allows you to quickly deploy scalable and secure Kubernetes clusters. By
sending requests to the `/v2/kubernetes/clusters` endpoint, you can list,
create, or delete clusters as well as scale node pools up and down,
recycle individual nodes, and retrieve the kubeconfig file for use with
a cluster.

## List All Kubernetes Clusters

<a id="opIdkubernetes_list_clusters"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/kubernetes/clusters \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/kubernetes/clusters`

To list all of the Kubernetes clusters on your account, send a GET request
to `/v2/kubernetes/clusters`.

## Create a New Kubernetes Cluster

<a id="opIdkubernetes_create_cluster"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/kubernetes/clusters \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "prod-cluster-01",
    "node_pools": [
      {
        "count": 3,
        "name": "worker-pool",
        "size": "s-1vcpu-2gb"
      }
    ],
    "region": "nyc1",
    "version": "1.18.6-do.0"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/kubernetes/clusters`

To create a new Kubernetes cluster, send a POST request to
`/v2/kubernetes/clusters`. The request must contain at least one node pool
with at least one worker.

The request may contain a maintenance window policy describing a time period
when disruptive maintenance tasks may be carried out. Omitting the policy
implies that a window will be chosen automatically. See
[here](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/kubernetes/how-to/upgrade-cluster/)
for details.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "prod-cluster-01",
  "node_pools": [
    {
      "count": 3,
      "name": "worker-pool",
      "size": "s-1vcpu-2gb"
    }
  ],
  "region": "nyc1",
  "version": "1.18.6-do.0"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-kubernetes-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» auto_upgrade|body|boolean|false|A boolean value indicating whether the cluster will be automatically upgraded to new patch releases during its maintenance window.|
|» ha|body|boolean|false|A boolean value indicating whether the control plane is run in a highly available configuration in the cluster. Highly available control planes incur less downtime. The property cannot be disabled.|
|» maintenance_policy|body|object \| null|false|An object specifying the maintenance window policy for the Kubernetes cluster.|
|» » day|body|string|false|The day of the maintenance window policy. May be one of `monday` through `sunday`, or `any` to indicate an arbitrary week day.|
|» » start_time|body|string|false|The start time in UTC of the maintenance window policy in 24-hour clock format / HH:MM notation (e.g., `15:00`).|
|» name|body|string|true|A human-readable name for a Kubernetes cluster.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The response will be a JSON object with a key called `kubernetes_cluster`. The<br>value of this will be an object containing the standard attributes of a<br>Kubernetes cluster.<br><br>The IP address and cluster API server endpoint will not be available until the<br>cluster has finished provisioning. The initial value of the cluster's<br>`status.state` attribute will be `provisioning`. When the cluster is ready,<br>this will transition to `running`.<br>|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|API Rate limit exceeded|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error.|Inline|
|default|Default|Unexpected error|Inline|

## Retrieve an Existing Kubernetes Cluster

to `/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID`.

## Update a Kubernetes Cluster

<a id="opIdkubernetes_update_cluster"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/kubernetes/clusters/bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "auto_upgrade": true,
    "ha": true,
    "maintenance_policy": {
      "day": "any",
      "start_time": "12:00"
    },
    "name": "prod-cluster-01",
    "surge_upgrade": true,
    "tags": [
      "k8s",
      "k8s:bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af",
      "production",
      "web-team"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/kubernetes/clusters/{cluster_id}`

To update a Kubernetes cluster, send a PUT request to
`/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID` and specify one or more of the
attributes below.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "auto_upgrade": true,
  "ha": true,
  "maintenance_policy": {
    "day": "any",
    "start_time": "12:00"
  },
  "name": "prod-cluster-01",
  "surge_upgrade": true,
  "tags": [
    "k8s",
    "k8s:bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af",
    "production",
    "web-team"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-kubernetes-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique ID that can be used to reference a Kubernetes cluster.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» auto_upgrade|body|boolean|false|A boolean value indicating whether the cluster will be automatically upgraded to new patch releases during its maintenance window.|
|» ha|body|boolean|false|A boolean value indicating whether the control plane is run in a highly available configuration in the cluster. Highly available control planes incur less downtime. The property cannot be disabled.|
|» maintenance_policy|body|object \| null|false|An object specifying the maintenance window policy for the Kubernetes cluster.|
|» » day|body|string|false|The day of the maintenance window policy. May be one of `monday` through `sunday`, or `any` to indicate an arbitrary week day.|
|» » start_time|body|string|false|The start time in UTC of the maintenance window policy in 24-hour clock format / HH:MM notation (e.g., `15:00`).|
|» name|body|string|true|A human-readable name for a Kubernetes cluster.|
|» surge_upgrade|body|boolean|false|A boolean value indicating whether surge upgrade is enabled/disabled for the cluster. Surge upgrade makes cluster upgrades fast and reliable by bringing up new nodes before destroying the outdated nodes.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|An array of tags applied to the Kubernetes cluster. All clusters are automatically tagged `k8s` and `k8s:$K8S_CLUSTER_ID`.|

## Delete a Kubernetes Cluster

<a id="opIdkubernetes_delete_cluster"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/kubernetes/clusters/bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/kubernetes/clusters/{cluster_id}`

To delete a Kubernetes cluster and all services deployed to it, send a DELETE
request to `/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID`.

A 204 status code with no body will be returned in response to a successful
request.


<h3 id="delete-a-kubernetes-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique ID that can be used to reference a Kubernetes cluster.|

```json
{

  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

```json

  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

```json
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
}
```

> default Response

```json
  "id": "example_error",

}
```

## Fetch Clusterlint Diagnostics for a Kubernetes Cluster

<a id="opIdkubernetes_get_clusterLintResults"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/kubernetes/clusters/bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af/clusterlint \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/kubernetes/clusters/{cluster_id}/clusterlint`

To request clusterlint diagnostics for your cluster, send a GET request to
`/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID/clusterlint`. If the `run_id` query
parameter is provided, then the diagnostics for the specific run is fetched.
By default, the latest results are shown.

To find out how to address clusterlint feedback, please refer to
[the clusterlint check documentation](https://github.com/digitalocean/clusterlint/blob/master/checks.md).


<h3 id="fetch-clusterlint-diagnostics-for-a-kubernetes-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique ID that can be used to reference a Kubernetes cluster.|
|run_id|query|string(uuid)|false|Specifies the clusterlint run whose results will be retrieved.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "completed_at": "2019-10-30T05:34:11Z",
  "diagnostics": [
    {
      "check_name": "unused-config-map",
      "message": "Unused config map",
      "object": {
        "kind": "config map",
        "name": "foo",
        "namespace": "kube-system"
      },
      "severity": "warning"
    }
  ],
  "requested_at": "2019-10-30T05:34:07Z",
  "run_id": "50c2f44c-011d-493e-aee5-361a4a0d1844"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h3 id="fetch-clusterlint-diagnostics-for-a-kubernetes-cluster-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The response is a JSON object which contains the diagnostics on Kubernetes<br>objects in the cluster. Each diagnostic will contain some metadata information<br>about the object and feedback for users to act upon.<br>|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|Inline|
|404|Not Found|The resource was not found.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|API Rate limit exceeded|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error.|Inline|
|default|Default|Unexpected error|Inline|

## Run Clusterlint Checks on a Kubernetes Cluster

<a id="opIdkubernetes_run_clusterLint"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/kubernetes/clusters/bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af/clusterlint \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "exclude_checks": [
      "default-namespace"
    ],
    "exclude_groups": [
      "workload-health"
    ],
    "include_checks": [
      "bare-pods",
      "resource-requirements"
    ],
    "include_groups": [
      "basic",
      "doks",
      "security"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/kubernetes/clusters/{cluster_id}/clusterlint`

Clusterlint helps operators conform to Kubernetes best practices around
resources, security and reliability to avoid common problems while operating
or upgrading the clusters.

To request a clusterlint run on your cluster, send a POST request to
`/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID/clusterlint`. This will run all
checks present in the `doks` group by default, if a request body is not
specified. Optionally specify the below attributes.

For information about the available checks, please refer to
[the clusterlint check documentation](https://github.com/digitalocean/clusterlint/blob/master/checks.md).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "exclude_checks": [
    "default-namespace"
  ],
  "exclude_groups": [
    "workload-health"
  ],
  "include_checks": [
    "bare-pods",
    "resource-requirements"
  ],
  "include_groups": [
    "basic",
    "doks",
    "security"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="run-clusterlint-checks-on-a-kubernetes-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique ID that can be used to reference a Kubernetes cluster.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» exclude_checks|body|[string]|false|An array of checks that will be run when clusterlint executes checks.|
|» exclude_groups|body|[string]|false|An array of check groups that will be omitted when clusterlint executes checks.|
|» include_checks|body|[string]|false|An array of checks that will be run when clusterlint executes checks.|
|» include_groups|body|[string]|false|An array of check groups that will be run when clusterlint executes checks.|

## Retrieve Credentials for a Kubernetes Cluster

<a id="opIdkubernetes_get_credentials"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/kubernetes/clusters/bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af/credentials \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/kubernetes/clusters/{cluster_id}/credentials`

This endpoint returns a JSON object . It can be used to programmatically
construct Kubernetes clients which cannot parse kubeconfig files.

The resulting JSON object contains token-based authentication for clusters
supporting it, and certificate-based authentication otherwise. For a list of
supported versions and more information, see "[How to Connect to a DigitalOcean
Kubernetes Cluster with kubectl](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/kubernetes/how-to/connect-with-kubectl/)".

To retrieve credentials for accessing a Kubernetes cluster, send a GET
request to `/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID/credentials`.

Clusters supporting token-based authentication may define an expiration by
passing a duration in seconds as a query parameter to
`/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID/kubeconfig?expiry_seconds=$DURATION_IN_SECONDS`.
If not set or 0, then the token will have a 7 day expiry. The query parameter
has no impact in certificate-based authentication.


<h3 id="retrieve-credentials-for-a-kubernetes-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique ID that can be used to reference a Kubernetes cluster.|
|expiry_seconds|query|integer|false|The duration in seconds that the returned Kubernetes credentials will be valid. If not set or 0, the credentials will have a 7 day expiry.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "certificate_authority_data": "",
  "client_certificate_data": null,
  "client_key_data": null,
  "expires_at": "2019-11-09T11:50:28.889080521Z",
  "server": "https://bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af.k8s.ondigitalocean.com",
  "token": "$DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

This is only returned for clusters<br>without support for token-based authentication.<br><br>Newly created Kubernetes clusters do not return credentials using<br>certificate-based authentication. ## Selectively Delete a Cluster and its Associated Resources

<a id="opIdkubernetes_destroy_associatedResourcesSelective"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/kubernetes/clusters/bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af/destroy_with_associated_resources/selective \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "load_balancers": [
      "4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6"
    ],
    "volume_snapshots": [
      "edb0478d-7436-11ea-86e6-0a58ac144b91"
    ],
    "volumes": [
      "ba49449a-7435-11ea-b89e-0a58ac14480f"
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /v2/kubernetes/clusters/{cluster_id}/destroy_with_associated_resources/selective`

To delete a Kubernetes cluster along with a subset of its associated resources,
send a DELETE request to `/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID/destroy_with_associated_resources/selective`.

The JSON body of the request should include `load_balancers`, `volumes`, or
`volume_snapshots` keys each set to an array of IDs for the associated
resources to be destroyed.

The IDs can be found by querying the cluster's associated resources endpoint.
Any associated resource not included in the request will remain and continue
to accrue changes on your account.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "load_balancers": [
    "4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6"
  ],
  "volume_snapshots": [
    "edb0478d-7436-11ea-86e6-0a58ac144b91"
  ],
  "volumes": [
    "ba49449a-7435-11ea-b89e-0a58ac14480f"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="selectively-delete-a-cluster-and-its-associated-resources-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique ID that can be used to reference a Kubernetes cluster.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» load_balancers|body|[string]|false|A list of IDs for associated load balancers to destroy along with the cluster.|
|» volume_snapshots|body|[string]|false|A list of IDs for associated volume snapshots to destroy along with the cluster.|
|» volumes|body|[string]|false|A list of IDs for associated volumes to destroy along with the cluster.|

## Retrieve the kubeconfig for a Kubernetes Cluster

<a id="opIdkubernetes_get_kubeconfig"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/kubernetes/clusters/bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af/kubeconfig \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/kubernetes/clusters/{cluster_id}/kubeconfig`

This endpoint returns a kubeconfig file in YAML format. It can be used to
connect to and administer the cluster using the Kubernetes command line tool,
`kubectl`, or other programs supporting kubeconfig files (e.g., client libraries).

The resulting kubeconfig file uses token-based authentication for clusters
supporting it, and certificate-based authentication otherwise. For a list of
supported versions and more information, see "[How to Connect to a DigitalOcean
Kubernetes Cluster with kubectl](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/kubernetes/how-to/connect-with-kubectl/)".

To retrieve a kubeconfig file for use with a Kubernetes cluster, send a GET
request to `/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID/kubeconfig`.

Clusters supporting token-based authentication may define an expiration by
passing a duration in seconds as a query parameter to
`/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID/kubeconfig?expiry_seconds=$DURATION_IN_SECONDS`.
If not set or 0, then the token will have a 7 day expiry. The query parameter
has no impact in certificate-based authentication.


<h3 id="retrieve-the-kubeconfig-for-a-kubernetes-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique ID that can be used to reference a Kubernetes cluster.|
|expiry_seconds|query|integer|false|The duration in seconds that the returned Kubernetes credentials will be valid. If not set or 0, the credentials will have a 7 day expiry.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```text
apiVersion: v1
clusters:
- cluster:
    certificate-authority-data: 
    server: https://bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af.k8s.ondigitalocean.com
  name: do-nyc1-prod-cluster-01
contexts:
- context:
    cluster: do-nyc1-prod-cluster-01
    user: do-nyc1-prod-cluster-01-admin
  name: do-nyc1-prod-cluster-01
current-context: do-nyc1-prod-cluster-01
kind: Config
preferences: {}
users:
- name: do-nyc1-prod-cluster-01-admin
  user:
    token: 403d085aaa80102277d8da97ffd2db2b6a4f129d0e2146098fdfb0cec624babc

```

<h3 id="list-all-node-pools-in-a-kubernetes-clusters-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|node_pools|[object]|false|none|none|
|» size|string|true|none|The slug identifier for the type of Droplet used as workers in the node pool.|
|» auto_scale|boolean|false|none|A boolean value indicating whether auto-scaling is enabled for this node pool.|
|» count|integer|true|none|The number of Droplet instances in the node pool.|
|» id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|A unique ID that can be used to identify and reference a specific node pool.|
|» labels|object \| null|false|none|An object containing a set of Kubernetes labels. The keys and are values are both user-defined.|
|» max_nodes|integer|false|none|The maximum number of nodes that this node pool can be auto-scaled to. The value will be `0` if `auto_scale` is set to `false`.|
|» min_nodes|integer|false|none|The minimum number of nodes that this node pool can be auto-scaled to. The value will be `0` if `auto_scale` is set to `false`.|
|» name|string|true|none|A human-readable name for the node pool.|
|» nodes|[object]|false|read-only|An object specifying the details of a specific worker node in a node pool.|
|» » created_at|string(date-time)|false|none|A time value given in ISO8601 combined date and time format that represents when the node was created.|
|» » droplet_id|string|false|none|The ID of the Droplet used for the worker node.|
|» » id|string(uuid)|false|none|A unique ID that can be used to identify and reference the node.|
|» » name|string|false|none|An automatically generated, human-readable name for the node.|
|» » status|object|false|none|An object containing a `state` attribute whose value is set to a string indicating the current status of the node.|
|» » » state|string|false|none|A string indicating the current status of the node.|
|» » updated_at|string(date-time)|false|none|A time value given in ISO8601 combined date and time format that represents when the node was last updated.|

|» taints|[object]|false|none|An array of taints to apply to all nodes in a pool. Taints will automatically be applied to all existing nodes and any subsequent nodes added to the pool. When a taint is removed, it is removed from all nodes in the pool.|

|» » value|string|false|none|An arbitrary string. The `key` and `value` fields of the `taint` object form a key-value pair. For example, if the value of the `key` field is "special" and the value of the `value` field is "gpu", the key value pair would be `special=gpu`.|

## Add a Node Pool to a Kubernetes Cluster

<a id="opIdkubernetes_add_nodePool"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/kubernetes/clusters/bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af/node_pools \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "auto_scale": true,
    "count": 3,
    "max_nodes": 6,
    "min_nodes": 3,
    "name": "new-pool",
    "size": "s-1vcpu-2gb",
    "tags": [
      "frontend"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/kubernetes/clusters/{cluster_id}/node_pools`

To add an additional node pool to a Kubernetes clusters, send a POST request
to `/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID/node_pools` with the following
attributes.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "auto_scale": true,
  "count": 3,
  "max_nodes": 6,
  "min_nodes": 3,
  "name": "new-pool",
  "size": "s-1vcpu-2gb",
  "tags": [
    "frontend"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-node-pool-to-a-kubernetes-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique ID that can be used to reference a Kubernetes cluster.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» size|body|string|true|The slug identifier for the type of Droplet used as workers in the node pool.|
|» auto_scale|body|boolean|false|A boolean value indicating whether auto-scaling is enabled for this node pool.|
|» count|body|integer|true|The number of Droplet instances in the node pool.|
|» labels|body|object \| null|false|An object containing a set of Kubernetes labels. The keys and are values are both user-defined.|
|» max_nodes|body|integer|false|The maximum number of nodes that this node pool can be auto-scaled to. The value will be `0` if `auto_scale` is set to `false`.|
|» min_nodes|body|integer|false|The minimum number of nodes that this node pool can be auto-scaled to. The value will be `0` if `auto_scale` is set to `false`.|
|» name|body|string|true|A human-readable name for the node pool.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|An array containing the tags applied to the node pool. All node pools are automatically tagged `k8s`, `k8s-worker`, and `k8s:$K8S_CLUSTER_ID`.|
|» taints|body|[object]|false|An array of taints to apply to all nodes in a pool. Taints will automatically be applied to all existing nodes and any subsequent nodes added to the pool. When a taint is removed, it is removed from all nodes in the pool.|
|» » effect|body|string|false|How the node reacts to pods that it won't tolerate. Available effect values are `NoSchedule`, `PreferNoSchedule`, and `NoExecute`.|
|» » key|body|string|false|An arbitrary string. The `key` and `value` fields of the `taint` object form a key-value pair. For example, if the value of the `key` field is "special" and the value of the `value` field is "gpu", the key value pair would be `special=gpu`.|
|» » value|body|string|false|An arbitrary string. The `key` and `value` fields of the `taint` object form a key-value pair. For example, if the value of the `key` field is "special" and the value of the `value` field is "gpu", the key value pair would be `special=gpu`.|

## Update a Node Pool in a Kubernetes Cluster

<a id="opIdkubernetes_update_nodePool"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/kubernetes/clusters/bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af/node_pools/cdda885e-7663-40c8-bc74-3a036c66545d \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "auto_scale": true,
    "count": 3,
    "labels": null,
    "max_nodes": 6,
    "min_nodes": 3,
    "name": "frontend-pool",
    "tags": [
      "k8s",
      "k8s:bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af",
      "k8s-worker",
      "production",
      "web-team"
    ],
    "taints": [
      {
        "effect": "NoSchedule",
        "key": "priority",
        "value": "high"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/kubernetes/clusters/{cluster_id}/node_pools/{node_pool_id}`

To update the name of a node pool, edit the tags applied to it, or adjust its
number of nodes, send a PUT request to
`/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID/node_pools/$NODE_POOL_ID` with the
following attributes.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "auto_scale": true,
  "count": 3,
  "labels": null,
  "max_nodes": 6,
  "min_nodes": 3,
  "name": "frontend-pool",
  "tags": [
    "k8s",
    "k8s:bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af",
    "k8s-worker",
    "production",
    "web-team"
  ],
  "taints": [
    {
      "effect": "NoSchedule",
      "key": "priority",
      "value": "high"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-node-pool-in-a-kubernetes-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique ID that can be used to reference a Kubernetes cluster.|
|node_pool_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique ID that can be used to reference a Kubernetes node pool.|
|body|body|object|true|none|

## Delete a Node Pool in a Kubernetes Cluster

<a id="opIdkubernetes_delete_nodePool"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/kubernetes/clusters/bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af/node_pools/cdda885e-7663-40c8-bc74-3a036c66545d \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/kubernetes/clusters/{cluster_id}/node_pools/{node_pool_id}`

To delete a node pool, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID/node_pools/$NODE_POOL_ID`.

A 204 status code with no body will be returned in response to a successful
request. Nodes in the pool will subsequently be drained and deleted.

|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique ID that can be used to reference a Kubernetes cluster.|
|node_pool_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique ID that can be used to reference a Kubernetes node pool.|

## Delete a Node in a Kubernetes Cluster

<a id="opIdkubernetes_delete_node"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/kubernetes/clusters/bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af/node_pools/cdda885e-7663-40c8-bc74-3a036c66545d/nodes/478247f8-b1bb-4f7a-8db9-2a5f8d4b8f8f \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/kubernetes/clusters/{cluster_id}/node_pools/{node_pool_id}/nodes/{node_id}`

To delete a single node in a pool, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID/node_pools/$NODE_POOL_ID/nodes/$NODE_ID`.

Appending the `skip_drain=1` query parameter to the request causes node
draining to be skipped. Omitting the query parameter or setting its value to
`0` carries out draining prior to deletion.

Appending the `replace=1` query parameter to the request causes the node to
be replaced by a new one after deletion. Omitting the query parameter or
setting its value to `0` deletes without replacement.


<h3 id="delete-a-node-in-a-kubernetes-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique ID that can be used to reference a Kubernetes cluster.|
|node_pool_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique ID that can be used to reference a Kubernetes node pool.|
|node_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique ID that can be used to reference a node in a Kubernetes node pool.|
|skip_drain|query|integer|false|Specifies whether or not to drain workloads from a node before it is deleted. Setting it to `1` causes node draining to be skipped. Omitting the query parameter or setting its value to `0` carries out draining prior to deletion.|
|replace|query|integer|false|Specifies whether or not to replace a node after it has been deleted. Setting it to `1` causes the node to be replaced by a new one after deletion. Omitting the query parameter or setting its value to `0` deletes without replacement.|

> Example responses

```json
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

```json
}
```

## Upgrade a Kubernetes Cluster

<a id="opIdkubernetes_upgrade_cluster"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/kubernetes/clusters/bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af/upgrade \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "version": "1.16.13-do.0"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/kubernetes/clusters/{cluster_id}/upgrade`

To immediately upgrade a Kubernetes cluster to a newer patch release of
Kubernetes, send a POST request to `/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID/upgrade`.
The body of the request must specify a version attribute.

Available upgrade versions for a cluster can be fetched from
`/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID/upgrades`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "version": "1.16.13-do.0"
}
```

<h3 id="upgrade-a-kubernetes-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique ID that can be used to reference a Kubernetes cluster.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» version|body|string|false|The slug identifier for the version of Kubernetes that the cluster will be upgraded to.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

`GET /v2/kubernetes/clusters/{cluster_id}/upgrades`

To determine whether a cluster can be upgraded, and the versions to which it
can be upgraded, send a GET request to
`/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID/upgrades`.

```json
      "kubernetes_version": "1.16.13",

        "cluster-autoscaler",
        "docr-integration",

}
```

## Retrieve User Information for a Kubernetes Cluster

<a id="opIdkubernetes_get_clusterUser"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/kubernetes/clusters/bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af/user \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/kubernetes/clusters/{cluster_id}/user`

To show information the user associated with a Kubernetes cluster, send a GET
request to `/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID/user`.


<h3 id="retrieve-user-information-for-a-kubernetes-cluster-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cluster_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique ID that can be used to reference a Kubernetes cluster.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "kubernetes_cluster_user": {
    "groups": [
      "k8saas:authenticated"
    ],
    "username": "sammy@digitalocean.com"
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-user-information-for-a-kubernetes-cluster-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The response will be a JSON object with a key called `kubernetes_cluster_user`<br>containing the username and in-cluster groups that it belongs to.<br>|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|Inline|
|404|Not Found|The resource was not found.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|API Rate limit exceeded|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error.|Inline|
|default|Default|Unexpected error|Inline|

## List Available Regions, Node Sizes, and Versions of Kubernetes

```bash
  -X POST \
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-load-balancers">Load Balancers</h1>

[DigitalOcean Load Balancers](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/networking/load-balancers/)
provide a way to distribute traffic across multiple Droplets. By sending
requests to the `/v2/load_balancers` endpoint, you can list, create, or
delete load balancers as well as add or remove Droplets, forwarding rules,
and other configuration details.

## List All Load Balancers

<a id="opIdloadBalancers_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/load_balancers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/load_balancers`

To list all of the load balancer instances on your account, send a GET request
to `/v2/load_balancers`.

## Create a New Load Balancer

<a id="opIdloadBalancers_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/load_balancers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "droplet_ids": [
      3164444,
      3164445
    ],
    "firewall": {
      "allow": [
        "ip:1.2.3.4",
        "cidr:2.3.4.0/24"
      ],
      "deny": [
        "cidr:1.2.0.0/16",
        "ip:2.3.4.5"
      ]
    },
    "forwarding_rules": [
      {
        "entry_port": 80,
        "entry_protocol": "http",
        "target_port": 80,
        "target_protocol": "http"
      },
      {
        "entry_port": 443,
        "entry_protocol": "https",
        "target_port": 443,
        "target_protocol": "https",
        "tls_passthrough": true
      }
    ],
    "http_idle_timeout_seconds": 60,
    "name": "example-lb-01",
    "project_id": "9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30",
    "region": "nyc3"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/load_balancers`

To create a new load balancer instance, send a POST request to
`/v2/load_balancers`.

You can specify the Droplets that will sit behind the load balancer using one
of two methods:

* Set `droplet_ids` to a list of specific Droplet IDs.
* Set `tag` to the name of a tag. All Droplets with this tag applied will be
  assigned to the load balancer. Additional Droplets will be automatically
  assigned as they are tagged.

These methods are mutually exclusive.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "droplet_ids": [
    3164444,
    3164445
  ],
  "firewall": {
    "allow": [
      "ip:1.2.3.4",
      "cidr:2.3.4.0/24"
    ],
    "deny": [
      "cidr:1.2.0.0/16",
      "ip:2.3.4.5"
    ]
  },
  "forwarding_rules": [
    {
      "entry_port": 80,
      "entry_protocol": "http",
      "target_port": 80,
      "target_protocol": "http"
    },
    {
      "entry_port": 443,
      "entry_protocol": "https",
      "target_port": 443,
      "target_protocol": "https",
      "tls_passthrough": true
    }
  ],
  "http_idle_timeout_seconds": 60,
  "name": "example-lb-01",
  "project_id": "9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30",
  "region": "nyc3"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-load-balancer-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **202**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|load_balancer|object|false|none|none|
|» algorithm|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** This field has been deprecated. You can no longer specify an algorithm for load balancers.|
|» created_at|string(date-time)|false|read-only|A time value given in ISO8601 combined date and time format that represents when the load balancer was created.|
|» disable_lets_encrypt_dns_records|boolean|false|none|A boolean value indicating whether to disable automatic DNS record creation for Let's Encrypt certificates that are added to the load balancer.|
|» enable_backend_keepalive|boolean|false|none|A boolean value indicating whether HTTP keepalive connections are maintained to target Droplets.|
|» enable_proxy_protocol|boolean|false|none|A boolean value indicating whether PROXY Protocol is in use.|
|» firewall|object|false|none|An object specifying allow and deny rules to control traffic to the load balancer.|
|» » allow|[string]|false|none|the rules for allowing traffic to the load balancer (in the form 'ip:1.2.3.4' or 'cidr:1.2.0.0/16')|
|» » deny|[string]|false|none|the rules for denying traffic to the load balancer (in the form 'ip:1.2.3.4' or 'cidr:1.2.0.0/16')|
|» forwarding_rules|[object]|true|none|An array of objects specifying the forwarding rules for a load balancer.|
|» » certificate_id|string|false|none|The ID of the TLS certificate used for SSL termination if enabled.|
|» » entry_port|integer|true|none|An integer representing the port on which the load balancer instance will listen.|
|» » entry_protocol|string|true|none|The protocol used for traffic to the load balancer. The possible values are: `http`, `https`, `http2`, `http3`, `tcp`, or `udp`. If you set the  `entry_protocol` to `udp`, the `target_protocol` must be set to `udp`.  When using UDP, the load balancer requires that you set up a health  check with a port that uses TCP, HTTP, or HTTPS to work properly.<br>|
|» » target_port|integer|true|none|An integer representing the port on the backend Droplets to which the load balancer will send traffic.|
|» » target_protocol|string|true|none|The protocol used for traffic from the load balancer to the backend Droplets. The possible values are: `http`, `https`, `http2`, `tcp`, or `udp`. If you set the `target_protocol` to `udp`, the `entry_protocol` must be set to  `udp`. When using UDP, the load balancer requires that you set up a health  check with a port that uses TCP, HTTP, or HTTPS to work properly.<br>|
|» » tls_passthrough|boolean|false|none|A boolean value indicating whether SSL encrypted traffic will be passed through to the backend Droplets.|
|» health_check|object|false|none|An object specifying health check settings for the load balancer.|
|» » check_interval_seconds|integer|false|none|The number of seconds between between two consecutive health checks.|
|» » healthy_threshold|integer|false|none|The number of times a health check must pass for a backend Droplet to be marked "healthy" and be re-added to the pool.|
|» » path|string|false|none|The path on the backend Droplets to which the load balancer instance will send a request.|
|» » port|integer|false|none|An integer representing the port on the backend Droplets on which the health check will attempt a connection.|
|» » protocol|string|false|none|The protocol used for health checks sent to the backend Droplets. The possible values are `http`, `https`, or `tcp`.|
|» » response_timeout_seconds|integer|false|none|The number of seconds the load balancer instance will wait for a response until marking a health check as failed.|
|» » unhealthy_threshold|integer|false|none|The number of times a health check must fail for a backend Droplet to be marked "unhealthy" and be removed from the pool.|
|» http_idle_timeout_seconds|integer|false|none|An integer value which configures the idle timeout for HTTP requests to the target droplets.|
|» id|string(uuid)|false|read-only|A unique ID that can be used to identify and reference a load balancer.|
|» ip|string|false|read-only|An attribute containing the public-facing IP address of the load balancer.|
|» name|string|false|none|A human-readable name for a load balancer instance.|
|» project_id|string|false|none|The ID of the project that the load balancer is associated with. If no ID is provided at creation, the load balancer associates with the user's default project. If an invalid project ID is provided, the load balancer will not be created.|
|» redirect_http_to_https|boolean|false|none|A boolean value indicating whether HTTP requests to the load balancer on port 80 will be redirected to HTTPS on port 443.|
|» size|string|false|none|**Deprecated.** This field has been replaced by the `size_unit` field for all regions except in AMS2, NYC2, and SFO1. Each available load balancer size now equates to the load balancer having a set number of nodes.<br>* `lb-small` = 1 node<br>* `lb-medium` = 3 nodes<br>* `lb-large` = 6 nodes<br><br>You can resize load balancers after creation up to once per hour. You cannot resize a load balancer within the first hour of its creation.|
|» size_unit|integer|false|none|How many nodes the load balancer contains. Each additional node increases the load balancer's ability to manage more connections. Load balancers can be scaled up or down, and you can change the number of nodes after creation up to once per hour. This field is currently not available in the AMS2, NYC2, or SFO1 regions. Use the `size` field to scale load balancers that reside in these regions.|
|» status|string|false|read-only|A status string indicating the current state of the load balancer. This can be `new`, `active`, or `errored`.|
|» sticky_sessions|object|false|none|An object specifying sticky sessions settings for the load balancer.|
|» » cookie_name|string|false|none|The name of the cookie sent to the client. This attribute is only returned when using `cookies` for the sticky sessions type.|
|» » cookie_ttl_seconds|integer|false|none|The number of seconds until the cookie set by the load balancer expires. This attribute is only returned when using `cookies` for the sticky sessions type.|
|» » type|string|false|none|An attribute indicating how and if requests from a client will be persistently served by the same backend Droplet. The possible values are `cookies` or `none`.|
|» vpc_uuid|string(uuid)|false|none|A string specifying the UUID of the VPC to which the load balancer is assigned.|
|» region|object|false|none|none|
|» » available|boolean|true|none|This is a boolean value that represents whether new Droplets can be created in this region.|
|» » features|[string]|true|none|This attribute is set to an array which contains features available in this region|
|» » name|string|true|none|The display name of the region.  This will be a full name that is used in the control panel and other interfaces.|
|» » sizes|[string]|true|none|This attribute is set to an array which contains the identifying slugs for the sizes available in this region.|
|» » slug|string|true|none|A human-readable string that is used as a unique identifier for each region.|
|» droplet_ids|[integer]|false|none|An array containing the IDs of the Droplets assigned to the load balancer.|
|» tag|string|false|none|The name of a Droplet tag corresponding to Droplets assigned to the load balancer.|

|» » target_port|integer|true|none|An integer representing the port on the backend Droplets to which the load balancer will send traffic.|
|» » target_protocol|string|true|none|The protocol used for traffic from the load balancer to the backend Droplets. The possible values are: `http`, `https`, `http2`, `tcp`, or `udp`. When using UDP, the load balancer requires that you set up a health  check with a port that uses TCP, HTTP, or HTTPS to work properly.<br>|

|» » check_interval_seconds|integer|false|none|The number of seconds between between two consecutive health checks.|
|» » healthy_threshold|integer|false|none|The number of times a health check must pass for a backend Droplet to be marked "healthy" and be re-added to the pool.|
|» » path|string|false|none|The path on the backend Droplets to which the load balancer instance will send a request.|
|» » port|integer|false|none|An integer representing the port on the backend Droplets on which the health check will attempt a connection.|
|» » protocol|string|false|none|The protocol used for health checks sent to the backend Droplets. The possible values are `http`, `https`, or `tcp`.|
|» » response_timeout_seconds|integer|false|none|The number of seconds the load balancer instance will wait for a response until marking a health check as failed.|
|» » unhealthy_threshold|integer|false|none|The number of times a health check must fail for a backend Droplet to be marked "unhealthy" and be removed from the pool.|
|» http_idle_timeout_seconds|integer|false|none|An integer value which configures the idle timeout for HTTP requests to the target droplets.|

|» ip|string|false|read-only|An attribute containing the public-facing IP address of the load balancer.|
|» name|string|false|none|A human-readable name for a load balancer instance.|

## Update a Load Balancer

<a id="opIdloadBalancers_update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/load_balancers/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "algorithm": "round_robin",
    "droplet_ids": [
      3164444,
      3164445
    ],
    "enable_backend_keepalive": true,
    "enable_proxy_protocol": true,
    "firewall": {
      "allow": [
        "ip:1.2.3.4",
        "cidr:2.3.4.0/24"
      ],
      "deny": [
        "cidr:1.2.0.0/16",
        "ip:2.3.4.5"
      ]
    },
    "forwarding_rules": [
      {
        "certificate_id": "",
        "entry_port": 80,
        "entry_protocol": "http",
        "target_port": 80,
        "target_protocol": "http",
        "tls_passthrough": false
      },
      {
        "certificate_id": "",
        "entry_port": 443,
        "entry_protocol": "https",
        "target_port": 443,
        "target_protocol": "https",
        "tls_passthrough": true
      }
    ],
    "health_check": {
      "check_interval_seconds": 10,
      "healthy_threshold": 5,
      "path": "/",
      "port": 80,
      "protocol": "http",
      "response_timeout_seconds": 5,
      "unhealthy_threshold": 3
    },
    "http_idle_timeout_seconds": 60,
    "name": "updated-example-lb-01",
    "project_id": "9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30",
    "redirect_http_to_https": false,
    "region": "nyc3",
    "sticky_sessions": {
      "type": "none"
    },
    "vpc_uuid": "c33931f2-a26a-4e61-b85c-4e95a2ec431b"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/load_balancers/{lb_id}`

To update a load balancer's settings, send a PUT request to
`/v2/load_balancers/$LOAD_BALANCER_ID`. The request should contain a full
representation of the load balancer including existing attributes. It may
contain _one of_ the `droplets_ids` or `tag` attributes as they are mutually
exclusive. **Note that any attribute that is not provided will be reset to its
default value.**


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "algorithm": "round_robin",
  "droplet_ids": [
    3164444,
    3164445
  ],
  "enable_backend_keepalive": true,
  "enable_proxy_protocol": true,
  "firewall": {
    "allow": [
      "ip:1.2.3.4",
      "cidr:2.3.4.0/24"
    ],
    "deny": [
      "cidr:1.2.0.0/16",
      "ip:2.3.4.5"
    ]
  },
  "forwarding_rules": [
    {
      "certificate_id": "",
      "entry_port": 80,
      "entry_protocol": "http",
      "target_port": 80,
      "target_protocol": "http",
      "tls_passthrough": false
    },
    {
      "certificate_id": "",
      "entry_port": 443,
      "entry_protocol": "https",
      "target_port": 443,
      "target_protocol": "https",
      "tls_passthrough": true
    }
  ],
  "health_check": {
    "check_interval_seconds": 10,
    "healthy_threshold": 5,
    "path": "/",
    "port": 80,
    "protocol": "http",
    "response_timeout_seconds": 5,
    "unhealthy_threshold": 3
  },
  "http_idle_timeout_seconds": 60,
  "name": "updated-example-lb-01",
  "project_id": "9cc10173-e9ea-4176-9dbc-a4cee4c4ff30",
  "redirect_http_to_https": false,
  "region": "nyc3",
  "sticky_sessions": {
    "type": "none"
  },
  "vpc_uuid": "c33931f2-a26a-4e61-b85c-4e95a2ec431b"
}
```

|» size_unit|body|integer|false|How many nodes the load balancer contains. Each additional node increases the load balancer's ability to manage more connections. Load balancers can be scaled up or down, and you can change the number of nodes after creation up to once per hour. This field is currently not available in the AMS2, NYC2, or SFO1 regions. Use the `size` field to scale load balancers that reside in these regions.|
|» sticky_sessions|body|object|false|An object specifying sticky sessions settings for the load balancer.|
|» » cookie_name|body|string|false|The name of the cookie sent to the client. This attribute is only returned when using `cookies` for the sticky sessions type.|
|» » cookie_ttl_seconds|body|integer|false|The number of seconds until the cookie set by the load balancer expires. This attribute is only returned when using `cookies` for the sticky sessions type.|
|» » type|body|string|false|An attribute indicating how and if requests from a client will be persistently served by the same backend Droplet. The possible values are `cookies` or `none`.|
|» vpc_uuid|body|string(uuid)|false|A string specifying the UUID of the VPC to which the load balancer is assigned.|

When using UDP, the load balancer requires that you set up a health  check with a port that uses TCP, HTTP, or HTTPS to work properly.<br>|
|» » target_port|integer|true|none|An integer representing the port on the backend Droplets to which the load balancer will send traffic.|
|» » target_protocol|string|true|none|The protocol used for traffic from the load balancer to the backend Droplets. The possible values are: `http`, `https`, `http2`, `tcp`, or `udp`. ## Delete a Load Balancer

<a id="opIdloadBalancers_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/load_balancers/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/load_balancers/{lb_id}`

To delete a load balancer instance, disassociating any Droplets assigned to it
and removing it from your account, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/load_balancers/$LOAD_BALANCER_ID`.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully.


<h3 id="delete-a-load-balancer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lb_id|path|string|true|A unique identifier for a load balancer.|

```json
}
```

## Add Droplets to a Load Balancer

<a id="opIdloadBalancers_add_droplets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/load_balancers/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6/droplets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "droplet_ids": [
      3164444,
      3164445
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/load_balancers/{lb_id}/droplets`

To assign a Droplet to a load balancer instance, send a POST request to
`/v2/load_balancers/$LOAD_BALANCER_ID/droplets`. In the body of the request,
there should be a `droplet_ids` attribute containing a list of Droplet IDs.
Individual Droplets can not be added to a load balancer configured with a
Droplet tag. Attempting to do so will result in a "422 Unprocessable Entity"
response from the API.

No response body will be sent back, but the response code will indicate
success. Specifically, the response code will be a 204, which means that the
action was successful with no returned body data.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "droplet_ids": [
    3164444,
    3164445
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-droplets-to-a-load-balancer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lb_id|path|string|true|A unique identifier for a load balancer.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» droplet_ids|body|[integer]|false|An array containing the IDs of the Droplets assigned to the load balancer.|

## Add Forwarding Rules to a Load Balancer

<a id="opIdloadBalancers_add_forwardingRules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/load_balancers/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6/forwarding_rules \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "forwarding_rules": [
      {
        "certificate_id": "892071a0-bb95-49bc-8021-3afd67a210bf",
        "entry_port": 443,
        "entry_protocol": "https",
        "target_port": 80,
        "target_protocol": "http",
        "tls_passthrough": false
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/load_balancers/{lb_id}/forwarding_rules`

To add an additional forwarding rule to a load balancer instance, send a POST
request to `/v2/load_balancers/$LOAD_BALANCER_ID/forwarding_rules`. In the body
of the request, there should be a `forwarding_rules` attribute containing an
array of rules to be added.

No response body will be sent back, but the response code will indicate
success. Specifically, the response code will be a 204, which means that the
action was successful with no returned body data.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "forwarding_rules": [
    {
      "certificate_id": "892071a0-bb95-49bc-8021-3afd67a210bf",
      "entry_port": 443,
      "entry_protocol": "https",
      "target_port": 80,
      "target_protocol": "http",
      "tls_passthrough": false
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-forwarding-rules-to-a-load-balancer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lb_id|path|string|true|A unique identifier for a load balancer.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» forwarding_rules|body|[object]|true|none|
|» » certificate_id|body|string|false|The ID of the TLS certificate used for SSL termination if enabled.|
|» » entry_port|body|integer|true|An integer representing the port on which the load balancer instance will listen.|
|» » entry_protocol|body|string|true|The protocol used for traffic to the load balancer. The possible values are: `http`, `https`, `http2`, `http3`, `tcp`, or `udp`. If you set the  `entry_protocol` to `udp`, the `target_protocol` must be set to `udp`.  When using UDP, the load balancer requires that you set up a health  check with a port that uses TCP, HTTP, or HTTPS to work properly.<br>|
|» » target_port|body|integer|true|An integer representing the port on the backend Droplets to which the load balancer will send traffic.|
|» » target_protocol|body|string|true|The protocol used for traffic from the load balancer to the backend Droplets. The possible values are: `http`, `https`, `http2`, `tcp`, or `udp`. If you set the `target_protocol` to `udp`, the `entry_protocol` must be set to  `udp`. When using UDP, the load balancer requires that you set up a health  check with a port that uses TCP, HTTP, or HTTPS to work properly.<br>|
|» » tls_passthrough|body|boolean|false|A boolean value indicating whether SSL encrypted traffic will be passed through to the backend Droplets.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » entry_protocol|http|
|» » entry_protocol|https|
|» » entry_protocol|http2|
|» » entry_protocol|http3|
|» » entry_protocol|tcp|
|» » entry_protocol|udp|
|» » target_protocol|http|
|» » target_protocol|https|
|» » target_protocol|http2|
|» » target_protocol|tcp|
|» » target_protocol|udp|

## Remove Forwarding Rules from a Load Balancer

<a id="opIdloadBalancers_remove_forwardingRules"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/load_balancers/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6/forwarding_rules \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "forwarding_rules": [
      {
        "certificate_id": "892071a0-bb95-49bc-8021-3afd67a210bf",
        "entry_port": 443,
        "entry_protocol": "https",
        "target_port": 80,
        "target_protocol": "http",
        "tls_passthrough": false
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /v2/load_balancers/{lb_id}/forwarding_rules`

To remove forwarding rules from a load balancer instance, send a DELETE
request to `/v2/load_balancers/$LOAD_BALANCER_ID/forwarding_rules`. In the
body of the request, there should be a `forwarding_rules` attribute containing
an array of rules to be removed.

No response body will be sent back, but the response code will indicate
success. Specifically, the response code will be a 204, which means that the
action was successful with no returned body data.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "forwarding_rules": [
    {
      "certificate_id": "892071a0-bb95-49bc-8021-3afd67a210bf",
      "entry_port": 443,
      "entry_protocol": "https",
      "target_port": 80,
      "target_protocol": "http",
      "tls_passthrough": false
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="remove-forwarding-rules-from-a-load-balancer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lb_id|path|string|true|A unique identifier for a load balancer.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» forwarding_rules|body|[object]|true|none|
|» » certificate_id|body|string|false|The ID of the TLS certificate used for SSL termination if enabled.|
|» » entry_port|body|integer|true|An integer representing the port on which the load balancer instance will listen.|
|» » entry_protocol|body|string|true|The protocol used for traffic to the load balancer. The possible values are: `http`, `https`, `http2`, `http3`, `tcp`, or `udp`. If you set the  `entry_protocol` to `udp`, the `target_protocol` must be set to `udp`.  When using UDP, the load balancer requires that you set up a health  check with a port that uses TCP, HTTP, or HTTPS to work properly.<br>|
|» » target_port|body|integer|true|An integer representing the port on the backend Droplets to which the load balancer will send traffic.|
|» » target_protocol|body|string|true|The protocol used for traffic from the load balancer to the backend Droplets. The possible values are: `http`, `https`, `http2`, `tcp`, or `udp`. If you set the `target_protocol` to `udp`, the `entry_protocol` must be set to  `udp`. When using UDP, the load balancer requires that you set up a health  check with a port that uses TCP, HTTP, or HTTPS to work properly.<br>|
|» » tls_passthrough|body|boolean|false|A boolean value indicating whether SSL encrypted traffic will be passed through to the backend Droplets.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » entry_protocol|http|
|» » entry_protocol|https|
|» » entry_protocol|http2|
|» » entry_protocol|http3|
|» » entry_protocol|tcp|
|» » entry_protocol|udp|
|» » target_protocol|http|
|» » target_protocol|https|
|» » target_protocol|http2|
|» » target_protocol|tcp|
|» » target_protocol|udp|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-monitoring">Monitoring</h1>

The DigitalOcean Monitoring API makes it possible to programmatically retrieve metrics as well as configure alert
policies based on these metrics. The Monitoring API can help you gain insight into how your apps are performing
and consuming resources.

## List Alert Policies

<a id="opIdmonitoring_list_alertPolicy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/monitoring/alerts \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/monitoring/alerts`

Returns all alert policies that are configured for the given account. To List all alert policies, send a GET request to `/v2/monitoring/alerts`.

<h3 id="list-alert-policies-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

## Create Alert Policy

<a id="opIdmonitoring_create_alertPolicy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/monitoring/alerts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "alerts": {
      "email": [
        "bob@exmaple.com"
      ],
      "slack": [
        {
          "channel": "Production Alerts",
          "url": "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T1234567/AAAAAAAA/ZZZZZZ"
        }
      ]
    },
    "compare": "GreaterThan",
    "description": "CPU Alert",
    "enabled": true,
    "entities": [
      "192018292"
    ],
    "tags": [
      "droplet_tag"
    ],
    "type": "v1/insights/droplet/cpu",
    "value": 80,
    "window": "5m"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/monitoring/alerts`

To create a new alert, send a POST request to `/v2/monitoring/alerts`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "alerts": {
    "email": [
      "bob@exmaple.com"
    ],
    "slack": [
      {
        "channel": "Production Alerts",
        "url": "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T1234567/AAAAAAAA/ZZZZZZ"
      }
    ]
  },
  "compare": "GreaterThan",
  "description": "CPU Alert",
  "enabled": true,
  "entities": [
    "192018292"
  ],
  "tags": [
    "droplet_tag"
  ],
  "type": "v1/insights/droplet/cpu",
  "value": 80,
  "window": "5m"
}
```

<h3 id="create-alert-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|The `type` field dictates what type of entity that the alert policy applies to and hence what type of entity is passed in the `entities` array. If both the `tags` array and `entities` array are empty the alert policy applies to all entities of the relevant type that are owned by the user account. load average \| Droplet ID<br>`v1/insights/droplet/disk_utilization_percent` \| alert on the percent of disk utilization \| Droplet ID<br>`v1/insights/droplet/cpu` \| alert on the percent of CPU percent of CPU utilization\|load balancer ID<br>`v1/insights/lbaas/connection_utilization_percent`\|alert on the percent of connection utilization\|load balancer ID<br>`v1/insights/lbaas/droplet_health`\|alert on Droplet health status changes\|load balancer ID<br>`v1/insights/lbaas/tls_connections_per_second_utilization_percent`\|alert on the percent of TLS ## Update an Alert Policy

<a id="opIdmonitoring_update_alertPolicy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/monitoring/alerts/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "alerts": {
      "email": [
        "bob@exmaple.com"
      ],
      "slack": [
        {
          "channel": "Production Alerts",
          "url": "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T1234567/AAAAAAAA/ZZZZZZ"
        }
      ]
    },
    "compare": "GreaterThan",
    "description": "CPU Alert",
    "enabled": true,
    "entities": [
      "192018292"
    ],
    "tags": [
      "droplet_tag"
    ],
    "type": "v1/insights/droplet/cpu",
    "value": 80,
    "window": "5m"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/monitoring/alerts/{alert_uuid}`

To update en existing policy, send a PUT request to `v2/monitoring/alerts/{alert_uuid}`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "alerts": {
    "email": [
      "bob@exmaple.com"
    ],
    "slack": [
      {
        "channel": "Production Alerts",
        "url": "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T1234567/AAAAAAAA/ZZZZZZ"
      }
    ]
  },
  "compare": "GreaterThan",
  "description": "CPU Alert",
  "enabled": true,
  "entities": [
    "192018292"
  ],
  "tags": [
    "droplet_tag"
  ],
  "type": "v1/insights/droplet/cpu",
  "value": 80,
  "window": "5m"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-alert-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|alert_uuid|path|string|true|A unique identifier for an alert policy.|
|body|body|object|true|The `type` field dictates what type of entity that the alert policy applies to and hence what type of entity is passed in the `entities` array. If both the `tags` array and `entities` array are empty the alert policy applies to all entities of the relevant type that are owned by the user account. Type<br>-----\|-------------\|--------------------<br>`v1/insights/droplet/memory_utilization_percent` \| alert on the percent of memory utilization \| Droplet ID<br>`v1/insights/droplet/disk_read` \|
