load average \| Droplet ID<br>`v1/insights/droplet/disk_utilization_percent` \| alert on the percent of disk utilization \| Droplet ID<br>`v1/insights/droplet/cpu` \| alert on the percent of CPU utilization \| Droplet ID<br>`v1/insights/droplet/disk_write` \| alert on the rate of disk write I/O in MBps \| Droplet ID<br>`v1/insights/droplet/public_outbound_bandwidth` \| alert on the rate of public outbound bandwidth in Mbps \| Droplet ID<br>`v1/insights/droplet/public_inbound_bandwidth` \| alert on the rate of public inbound bandwidth in Mbps \| Droplet ID<br>`v1/insights/droplet/private_outbound_bandwidth` \| alert on the rate of private outbound bandwidth in Mbps \| Droplet ID<br>`v1/insights/droplet/private_inbound_bandwidth` \| alert on the rate of private inbound bandwidth in Mbps \| Droplet ID<br>`v1/insights/droplet/load_1` \| alert on the 1 minute load average \| Droplet ID<br>`v1/insights/lbaas/avg_cpu_utilization_percent`\|alert on the percent of CPU utilization\|load balancer ID<br>`v1/insights/lbaas/connection_utilization_percent`\|alert on the percent of connection utilization\|load balancer ID<br>`v1/insights/lbaas/droplet_health`\|alert on Droplet health status changes\|load balancer ID<br>`v1/insights/lbaas/tls_connections_per_second_utilization_percent`\|alert on the percent of TLS ## Delete an Alert Policy

<a id="opIdmonitoring_delete_alertPolicy"></a>

## Get Droplet Bandwidth Metrics

<a id="opIdmonitoring_get_dropletBandwidthMetrics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/v2/monitoring/metrics/droplet/bandwidth?host_id=17209102&interface=private&direction=inbound&start=1620683817&end=1620705417' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/monitoring/metrics/droplet/bandwidth`

To retrieve bandwidth metrics for a given Droplet, send a GET request to `/v2/monitoring/metrics/droplet/bandwidth`. Use the `interface` query parameter to specify if the results should be for the `private` or `public` interface. Use the `direction` query parameter to specify if the results should be for `inbound` or `outbound` traffic.

<h3 id="get-droplet-bandwidth-metrics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|host_id|query|string|true|The droplet ID.|
|interface|query|string|true|The network interface.|
|direction|query|string|true|The traffic direction.|
|start|query|string|true|Timestamp to start metric window.|
|end|query|string|true|Timestamp to end metric window.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|interface|private|
|interface|public|
|direction|inbound|
|direction|outbound|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-project-resources">Project Resources</h1>

Project Resources are resources that can be grouped into your projects.
You can group resources (like Droplets, Spaces, load balancers, domains,
and floating IPs) in ways that align with the applications you host on
DigitalOcean.

### Supported Resource Types Examples

Projects resources are identified by uniform resource names or URNs. A
valid URN has the following format: `do:resource_type:resource_id`. The
following resource types are supported:

Resource Type      | Example URN
-------------------|------------
App Platform App   | `do:app:be5aab85-851b-4cab-b2ed-98d5a63ba4e8`
Database           | `do:dbaas:83c7a55f-0d84-4760-9245-aba076ec2fb2`
Domain             | `do:domain:example.com`
Droplet            | `do:droplet:4126873`
Floating IP        | `do:floatingip:192.168.99.100`
Kubernetes Cluster | `do:kubernetes:bd5f5959-5e1e-4205-a714-a914373942af`
Load Balancer      | `do:loadbalancer:39052d89-8dd4-4d49-8d5a-3c3b6b365b5b`
Space              | `do:space:my-website-assets`
Volume             | `do:volume:6fc4c277-ea5c-448a-93cd-dd496cfef71f`

### Resource Status Codes

When assigning and retrieving resources in projects, a `status` attribute
is returned that indicates if a resource was successfully retrieved or
assigned. The status codes can be one of the following:

Status Code        | Explanation
-------------------|------------
`ok`               | There was no problem retrieving or assigning a resource.
`not_found`        | The resource was not found.
`assigned`         | The resource was successfully assigned.
`already_assigned` | The resource was already assigned.
`service_down`     | There was a problem retrieving or assigning a resource. Please try again.

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-projects">Projects</h1>

Projects allow you to organize your resources into groups that fit the way
you work. You can group resources (like Droplets, Spaces, load balancers,
domains, and floating IPs) in ways that align with the applications
you host on DigitalOcean.

## List All Projects

<a id="opIdprojects_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/projects \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/projects`

To list all your projects, send a GET request to `/v2/projects`.

|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

## Create a Project

<a id="opIdprojects_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/projects \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "My website API",
    "environment": "Production",
    "name": "my-web-api",
    "purpose": "Service or API"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/projects`

To create a project, send a POST request to `/v2/projects`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "My website API",
  "environment": "Production",
  "name": "my-web-api",
  "purpose": "Service or API"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the project. The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|» environment|body|string|false|The environment of the project's resources.|
|» name|body|string|true|The human-readable name for the project. The maximum length is 175 characters and the name must be unique.|
|» purpose|body|string|true|The purpose of the project. The maximum length is 255 characters. It can<br>have one of the following values:<br><br>- Just trying out DigitalOcean<br>- Class project / Educational purposes<br>- Website or blog<br>- Web Application<br>- Service or API<br>- Mobile Application<br>- Machine learning / AI / Data processing<br>- IoT<br>- Operational / Developer tooling<br><br>If another value for purpose is specified, for example, "your custom purpose",<br>your purpose will be stored as `Other: your custom purpose`.<br>|

|---|---|
|» environment|Development|
|» environment|Staging|
|» environment|Production|

## Update the Default Project

<a id="opIdprojects_update_default"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/projects/default \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "My website API",
    "environment": "Production",
    "name": "my-web-api",
    "purpose": "Service or API",
    "is_default": false
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/projects/default`

To update you default project, send a PUT request to `/v2/projects/default`. All of the following attributes must be sent.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "My website API",
  "environment": "Production",
  "name": "my-web-api",
  "purpose": "Service or API",
  "is_default": false
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|body|body|object|true|none|

|» environment|body|string|true|The environment of the project's resources.|
|» name|body|string|true|The human-readable name for the project. The maximum length is 175 characters and the name must be unique.|
|» purpose|body|string|true|The purpose of the project. The maximum length is 255 characters. It can<br>have one of the following values:<br><br>- Just trying out DigitalOcean<br>- Class project / Educational purposes<br>- Website or blog<br>- Web Application<br>- Service or API<br>- Mobile Application<br>- Machine learning / AI / Data processing<br>- IoT<br>- Operational / Developer tooling<br><br>If another value for purpose is specified, for example, "your custom purpose",<br>your purpose will be stored as `Other: your custom purpose`.<br>|

## Update a Project

<a id="opIdprojects_update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/projects/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "My website API",
    "environment": "Production",
    "name": "my-web-api",
    "purpose": "Service or API",
    "is_default": false
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/projects/{project_id}`

To update a project, send a PUT request to `/v2/projects/$PROJECT_ID`. All of the following attributes must be sent.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "My website API",
  "environment": "Production",
  "name": "my-web-api",
  "purpose": "Service or API",
  "is_default": false
}
```

|» environment|body|string|true|The environment of the project's resources.|
|» name|body|string|true|The human-readable name for the project. The maximum length is 175 characters and the name must be unique.|

It can<br>have one of the following values:<br><br>- Just trying out DigitalOcean<br>- Class project / Educational purposes<br>- Website or blog<br>- Web Application<br>- Service or API<br>- Mobile Application<br>- Machine learning / AI / Data processing<br>- IoT<br>- Operational / Developer tooling<br><br>If another value for purpose is specified, for example, "your custom purpose",<br>your purpose will be stored as `Other: your custom purpose`.<br>|

## Delete an Existing Project

<a id="opIdprojects_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/projects/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/projects/{project_id}`

To delete a project, send a DELETE request to `/v2/projects/$PROJECT_ID`. To
be deleted, a project must not have any resources assigned to it. Any existing
resources must first be reassigned or destroyed, or you will receive a 412 error.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully.


<h3 id="delete-an-existing-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a project.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 412 Response

```json
{
  "id": "precondition_failed",
  "message": "cannot delete a project with resources. move or remove the resources first"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Patch a Project

<a id="opIdprojects_patch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/projects/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "my-web-api"
  }'
```

`PATCH /v2/projects/{project_id}`

To update only specific attributes of a project, send a PATCH request to `/v2/projects/$PROJECT_ID`. At least one of the following attributes needs to be sent.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "my-web-api"
}
```

<h3 id="patch-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|project_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a project.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|The description of the project. The maximum length is 255 characters.|
|» environment|body|string|false|The environment of the project's resources.|
|» name|body|string|false|The human-readable name for the project. The maximum length is 175 characters and the name must be unique.|
|» purpose|body|string|false|The purpose of the project. The maximum length is 255 characters. It can<br>have one of the following values:<br><br>- Just trying out DigitalOcean<br>- Class project / Educational purposes<br>- Website or blog<br>- Web Application<br>- Service or API<br>- Mobile Application<br>- Machine learning / AI / Data processing<br>- IoT<br>- Operational / Developer tooling<br><br>If another value for purpose is specified, for example, "your custom purpose",<br>your purpose will be stored as `Other: your custom purpose`.<br>|
|» is_default|body|boolean|false|If true, all resources will be added to this project if no project is specified.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» environment|Development|
|» environment|Staging|
|» environment|Production|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "project": {
    "created_at": "2018-09-27T20:10:35Z",
    "description": "My website API",
    "environment": "Production",
    "id": "4e1bfbc3-dc3e-41f2-a18f-1b4d7ba71679",
    "name": "my-web-api",
    "owner_id": 258992,
    "owner_uuid": "99525febec065ca37b2ffe4f852fd2b2581895e7",
    "purpose": "Service or API",
    "updated_at": "2018-09-27T20:10:35Z",
    "is_default": false
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-regions">Regions</h1>

Provides information about DigitalOcean data center regions.

## List All Data Center Regions

<a id="opIdregions_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/regions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/regions`

To list all of the regions that are available, send a GET request to `/v2/regions`.
The response will be a JSON object with a key called `regions`. The value of this will be an array of `region` objects, each of which will contain the standard region attributes.

<h3 id="list-all-data-center-regions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-reserved-ip-actions">Reserved IP Actions</h1>

As of 16 June 2022, we have renamed the [Floating IP](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/api-reference/#tag/Floating-IPs)
product to Reserved IPs. The Reserved IP product's endpoints function the exact
same way as Floating IPs. The only difference is the name change throughout the
URLs and fields. For example, the `floating_ips` field is now the `reserved_ips` field.
The Floating IP endpoints will remain active until fall 2023 before being
permanently deprecated.

With the exception of the [Projects API](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/api-reference/#tag/Projects),
we will reflect this change as an additional field in the responses across the API
where the `floating_ip` field is used. For example, the Droplet metadata response
will contain the field `reserved_ips` in addition to the `floating_ips` field.
Floating IPs retrieved using the Projects API will retain the original name.

Reserved IP actions are commands that can be given to a DigitalOcean
reserved IP. These requests are made on the actions endpoint of a specific
reserved IP.

An action object is returned. These objects hold the current status of the
requested action.

## List All Actions for a Reserved IP

<a id="opIdreservedIPsActions_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/reserved_ips/45.55.96.47/actions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/reserved_ips/{reserved_ip}/actions`

To retrieve all actions that have been executed on a reserved IP, send a GET request to `/v2/reserved_ips/$RESERVED_IP/actions`.

## Initiate a Reserved IP Action

<a id="opIdreservedIPsActions_post"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/reserved_ips/45.55.96.47/actions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "assign"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/reserved_ips/{reserved_ip}/actions`

To initiate an action on a reserved IP send a POST request to
`/v2/reserved_ips/$RESERVED_IP/actions`. In the JSON body to the request,
set the `type` attribute to on of the supported action types:

| Action     | Details
|------------|--------
| `assign`   | Assigns a reserved IP to a Droplet
| `unassign` | Unassign a reserved IP from a Droplet


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "assign"
}
```

<h3 id="initiate-a-reserved-ip-action-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|reserved_ip|path|string(ipv4)|true|A reserved IP address.|
|body|body|object|false|The `type` attribute set in the request body will specify the action that<br>will be taken on the reserved IP.<br>|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of action to initiate for the reserved IP.|
|» *anyOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of action to initiate for the reserved IP.|
|» droplet_id|body|integer|true|The ID of the Droplet that the reserved IP will be assigned to.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|assign|
|» type|unassign|
|» type|assign|
|» type|unassign|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-reserved-ips">Reserved IPs</h1>

As of 16 June 2022, we have renamed the [Floating IP](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/api-reference/#tag/Floating-IPs)
product to Reserved IPs. The Reserved IP product's endpoints function the exact
same way as Floating IPs. The only difference is the name change throughout the
URLs and fields. For example, the `floating_ips` field is now the `reserved_ips` field.
The Floating IP endpoints will remain active until fall 2023 before being
permanently deprecated.

With the exception of the [Projects API](https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/api-reference/#tag/Projects),
we will reflect this change as an additional field in the responses across the API
where the `floating_ip` field is used. For example, the Droplet metadata response
will contain the field `reserved_ips` in addition to the `floating_ips` field.
Floating IPs retrieved using the Projects API will retain the original name.

DigitalOcean Reserved IPs are publicly-accessible static IP addresses that can be
mapped to one of your Droplets. They can be used to create highly available
setups or other configurations requiring movable addresses.

Reserved IPs are bound to a specific region.

## Create a New Reserved IP

<a id="opIdreservedIPs_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/reserved_ips \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "droplet_id": 2457247
  }'
```

`POST /v2/reserved_ips`

On creation, a reserved IP must be either assigned to a Droplet or reserved to a region.
* To create a new reserved IP assigned to a Droplet, send a POST
  request to `/v2/reserved_ips` with the `droplet_id` attribute.

* To create a new reserved IP reserved to a region, send a POST request to
  `/v2/reserved_ips` with the `region` attribute.

**Note**:  In addition to the standard rate limiting, only 12 reserved IPs may be created per 60 seconds.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "droplet_id": 2457247
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-reserved-ip-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» droplet_id|body|integer|true|The ID of the Droplet that the reserved IP will be assigned to.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» project_id|body|string(uuid)|false|The UUID of the project to which the reserved IP will be assigned.|
|» region|body|string|true|The slug identifier for the region the reserved IP will be reserved to.|

## Retrieve an Existing Reserved IP

<a id="opIdreservedIPs_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/reserved_ips/45.55.96.47 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/reserved_ips/{reserved_ip}`

To show information about a reserved IP, send a GET request to `/v2/reserved_ips/$RESERVED_IP_ADDR`.

<h3 id="retrieve-an-existing-reserved-ip-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|reserved_ip|path|string(ipv4)|true|A reserved IP address.|

## Delete a Reserved IP

<a id="opIdreservedIPs_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/reserved_ips/45.55.96.47 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/reserved_ips/{reserved_ip}`

To delete a reserved IP and remove it from your account, send a DELETE request
to `/v2/reserved_ips/$RESERVED_IP_ADDR`.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully.

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-sizes">Sizes</h1>

The sizes objects represent different packages of hardware resources that
can be used for Droplets. When a Droplet is created, a size must be
selected so that the correct resources can be allocated.

Each size represents a plan that bundles together specific sets of
resources. This includes the amount of RAM, the number of virtual CPUs,
disk space, and transfer. The size object also includes the pricing
details and the regions that the size is available in.

## List All Droplet Sizes

<a id="opIdsizes_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/sizes \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/sizes`

To list all of available Droplet sizes, send a GET request to `/v2/sizes`.
The response will be a JSON object with a key called `sizes`. The value of this will be an array of `size` objects each of which contain the standard size attributes.

<h3 id="list-all-droplet-sizes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-snapshots">Snapshots</h1>

[Snapshots](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/images/snapshots/) are saved
instances of a Droplet or a block storage volume, which is reflected in
the `resource_type` attribute. In order to avoid problems with compressing
filesystems, each defines a `min_disk_size` attribute which is the minimum
size of the Droplet or volume disk when creating a new resource from the
saved snapshot.

To interact with snapshots, you will generally send requests to the
snapshots endpoint at `/v2/snapshots`.

## List All Snapshots

<a id="opIdsnapshots_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/snapshots \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/snapshots`

To list all of the snapshots available on your account, send a GET request to
`/v2/snapshots`.

The response will be a JSON object with a key called `snapshots`. This will be
set to an array of `snapshot` objects, each of which will contain the standard
snapshot attributes.

### Filtering Results by Resource Type

It's possible to request filtered results by including certain query parameters.

#### List Droplet Snapshots

To retrieve only snapshots based on Droplets, include the `resource_type`
query parameter set to `droplet`. For example, `/v2/snapshots?resource_type=droplet`.

#### List Volume Snapshots

To retrieve only snapshots based on volumes, include the `resource_type`
query parameter set to `volume`. For example, `/v2/snapshots?resource_type=volume`.


<h3 id="list-all-snapshots-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|
|resource_type|query|string|false|Used to filter snapshots by a resource type.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|resource_type|droplet|
|resource_type|volume|

## Retrieve an Existing Snapshot

<a id="opIdsnapshots_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/snapshots/6372321 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/snapshots/{snapshot_id}`

To retrieve information about a snapshot, send a GET request to
`/v2/snapshots/$SNAPSHOT_ID`.

The response will be a JSON object with a key called `snapshot`. The value of
this will be an snapshot object containing the standard snapshot attributes.


<h3 id="retrieve-an-existing-snapshot-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|snapshot_id|path|integer \| string|true|Either the ID of an existing snapshot. This will be an integer for a Droplet snapshot or a string for a volume snapshot.|

```json
      "nyc3",
      "sfo3"
    ],

    "resource_type": "droplet",
    "tags": [
```

## Delete a Snapshot

<a id="opIdsnapshots_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/snapshots/6372321 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/snapshots/{snapshot_id}`

Both Droplet and volume snapshots are managed through the `/v2/snapshots/`
endpoint. To delete a snapshot, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/snapshots/$SNAPSHOT_ID`.

A status of 204 will be given. This indicates that the request was processed
successfully, but that no response body is needed.


<h3 id="delete-a-snapshot-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|snapshot_id|path|integer \| string|true|Either the ID of an existing snapshot. This will be an integer for a Droplet snapshot or a string for a volume snapshot.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-ssh-keys">SSH Keys</h1>

Manage SSH keys available on your account.

## List All SSH Keys

<a id="opIdsshKeys_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/account/keys \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/account/keys`

To list all of the keys in your account, send a GET request to `/v2/account/keys`. The response will be a JSON object with a key set to `ssh_keys`. The value of this will be an array of ssh_key objects, each of which contains the standard ssh_key attributes.

<h3 id="list-all-ssh-keys-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "links": {},
  "meta": {
    "total": 1
  },
  "ssh_keys": [
    {
      "fingerprint": "3b:16:e4:bf:8b:00:8b:b8:59:8c:a9:d3:f0:19:fa:45",
      "id": 289794,
      "name": "Other Public Key",
      "public_key": "ssh-rsa ANOTHEREXAMPLEaC1yc2EAAAADAQABAAAAQQDDHr/jh2Jy4yALcK4JyWbVkPRaWmhck3IgCoeOO3z1e2dBowLh64QAM+Qb72pxekALga2oi4GvT+TlWNhzPH4V anotherexample"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Create a New SSH Key

<a id="opIdsshKeys_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/account/keys \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "My SSH Public Key",
    "public_key": "ssh-rsa AEXAMPLEaC1yc2EAAAADAQABAAAAQQDDHr/jh2Jy4yALcK4JyWbVkPRaWmhck3IgCoeOO3z1e2dBowLh64QAM+Qb72pxekALga2oi4GvT+TlWNhzPH4V example"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/account/keys`

To add a new SSH public key to your DigitalOcean account, send a POST request to `/v2/account/keys`. Set the `name` attribute to the name you wish to use and the `public_key` attribute to the full public key you are adding.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "My SSH Public Key",
  "public_key": "ssh-rsa AEXAMPLEaC1yc2EAAAADAQABAAAAQQDDHr/jh2Jy4yALcK4JyWbVkPRaWmhck3IgCoeOO3z1e2dBowLh64QAM+Qb72pxekALga2oi4GvT+TlWNhzPH4V example"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-ssh-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|A human-readable display name for this key, used to easily identify the SSH keys when they are displayed.|
|» public_key|body|string|true|The entire public key string that was uploaded. Embedded into the root user's `authorized_keys` file if you include this key during Droplet creation.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "ssh_key": {
    "fingerprint": "3b:16:bf:e4:8b:00:8b:b8:59:8c:a9:d3:f0:19:45:fa",
    "id": 512189,
    "name": "My SSH Public Key",
    "public_key": "ssh-rsa AEXAMPLEaC1yc2EAAAADAQABAAAAQQDDHr/jh2Jy4yALcK4JyWbVkPRaWmhck3IgCoeOO3z1e2dBowLh64QAM+Qb72pxekALga2oi4GvT+TlWNhzPH4V example"
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Retrieve an Existing SSH Key

<a id="opIdsshKeys_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/account/keys/512189 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/account/keys/{ssh_key_identifier}`

To get information about a key, send a GET request to `/v2/account/keys/$KEY_ID` or `/v2/account/keys/$KEY_FINGERPRINT`.
The response will be a JSON object with the key `ssh_key` and value an ssh_key object which contains the standard ssh_key attributes.

## Update an SSH Key's Name

<a id="opIdsshKeys_update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/account/keys/512189 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "My SSH Public Key"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/account/keys/{ssh_key_identifier}`

To update the name of an SSH key, send a PUT request to either `/v2/account/keys/$SSH_KEY_ID` or `/v2/account/keys/$SSH_KEY_FINGERPRINT`. Set the `name` attribute to the new name you want to use.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "My SSH Public Key"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-ssh-keys-name-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ssh_key_identifier|path|integer \| string|true|Either the ID or the fingerprint of an existing SSH key.|
|body|body|object|true|Set the `name` attribute to the new name you want to use.|
|» name|body|string|false|A human-readable display name for this key, used to easily identify the SSH keys when they are displayed.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response


## Delete an SSH Key

<a id="opIdsshKeys_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/account/keys/512189 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/account/keys/{ssh_key_identifier}`

To destroy a public SSH key that you have in your account, send a DELETE request to `/v2/account/keys/$KEY_ID` or `/v2/account/keys/$KEY_FINGERPRINT`.
A 204 status will be returned, indicating that the action was successful and that the response body is empty.

<h3 id="delete-an-ssh-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|ssh_key_identifier|path|integer \| string|true|Either the ID or the fingerprint of an existing SSH key.|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-tags">Tags</h1>

A tag is a label that can be applied to a resource (currently Droplets,
Images, Volumes, Volume Snapshots, and Database clusters) in order to
better organize or facilitate the lookups and actions on it.

Tags have two attributes: a user defined `name` attribute and an embedded
`resources` attribute with information about resources that have been tagged.

## List All Tags

<a id="opIdtags_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/tags \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/tags`

To list all of your tags, you can send a GET request to `/v2/tags`.

<h3 id="list-all-tags-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "links": {},
  "meta": {
    "total": 1
  },
  "tags": [
    {
      "name": "extra-awesome",
      "resources": {
        "count": 5,
        "databases": {
          "count": 1,
          "last_tagged_uri": "https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/databases/b92438f6-ba03-416c-b642-e9236db91976"
        },
        "droplets": {
          "count": 1,
          "last_tagged_uri": "https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/droplets/3164444"
        },

        },
        "last_tagged_uri": "https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/images/7555620",
        "volume_snapshots": {
          "count": 1,
          "last_tagged_uri": "https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/snapshots/1f6f46e8-6b60-11e9-be4e-0a58ac144519"
        },
        "volumes": {
          "count": 1,
          "last_tagged_uri": "https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/volumes/3d80cb72-342b-4aaa-b92e-4e4abb24a933"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
```

## Create a New Tag

<a id="opIdtags_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/tags \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "extra-awesome"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/tags`

To create a tag you can send a POST request to `/v2/tags` with a `name` attribute.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "extra-awesome"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-tag-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the tag. Tags may contain letters, numbers, colons, dashes, and underscores.<br>There is a limit of 255 characters per tag.<br><br>**Note:** Tag names are case stable, which means the capitalization you use when you first create a tag is canonical.<br><br>When working with tags in the API, you must use the tag's canonical capitalization. For example, if you create a tag named "PROD", the URL to add that tag to a resource would be `https://api.digitalocean.com/v2/tags/PROD/resources` (not `/v2/tags/prod/resources`).<br><br>Tagged resources in the control panel will always display the canonical capitalization. For example, if you create a tag named "PROD", you can tag resources in the control panel by entering "prod". The tag will still display with its canonical capitalization, "PROD".<br>|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "tag": {
    "name": "extra-awesome",
    "resources": {
      "count": 0,
      "databases": {
        "count": 0
      },
      "droplets": {
        "count": 0
      },
      "images": {
        "count": 0
      },
      "volume_snapshots": {
        "count": 0
      },
      "volumes": {
        "count": 0
      }
    }
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": "Error validating resource tag: \\\"tag-name \\\\\\\"здорово\\\\\\\" contains invalid characters\\\"",
  "messages": null,
  "root_causes": [
    "rpc error: code = InvalidArgument desc = Error validating resource tag: \\\"tag-name \\\\\\\"здорово\\\\\\\" contains invalid characters\\\""
  ]
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## Delete a Tag

<a id="opIdtags_delete"></a>

```bash

  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
```

`DELETE /v2/tags/{tag_id}`

A tag can be deleted by sending a `DELETE` request to `/v2/tags/$TAG_NAME`. Deleting a tag also untags all the resources that have previously been tagged by the Tag

## Tag a Resource

<a id="opIdtags_assign_resources"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/tags/awesome/resources \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "resources": [
      {
        "resource_id": "9569411",
        "resource_type": "droplet"
      },
      {
        "resource_id": "7555620",
        "resource_type": "image"
      },
      {
        "resource_id": "3d80cb72-342b-4aaa-b92e-4e4abb24a933",
        "resource_type": "volume"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v2/tags/{tag_id}/resources`

Resources can be tagged by sending a POST request to `/v2/tags/$TAG_NAME/resources` with an array of json objects containing `resource_id` and `resource_type` attributes.
Currently only tagging of Droplets, Databases, Images, Volumes, and Volume Snapshots is supported. `resource_type` is expected to be the string `droplet`, `database`, `image`, `volume` or `volume_snapshot`. `resource_id` is expected to be the ID of the resource as a string.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "resources": [
    {
      "resource_id": "9569411",
      "resource_type": "droplet"
    },
    {
      "resource_id": "7555620",
      "resource_type": "image"
    },
    {
      "resource_id": "3d80cb72-342b-4aaa-b92e-4e4abb24a933",
      "resource_type": "volume"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="tag-a-resource-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tag_id|path|string|true|The name of the tag. Tags may contain letters, numbers, colons, dashes, and underscores. There is a limit of 255 characters per tag.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» resources|body|[object]|true|An array of objects containing resource_id and resource_type  attributes.|
|» » resource_id|body|string|false|The identifier of a resource.|
|» » resource_type|body|string|false|The type of the resource.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » resource_type|droplet|
|» » resource_type|image|
|» » resource_type|volume|
|» » resource_type|volume_snapshot|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-uptime">Uptime</h1>

[DigitalOcean Uptime Checks](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/uptime/) provide the ability to monitor your endpoints from around the world, and alert you when they're slow, unavailable, or SSL certificates are expiring.
To interact with Uptime, you will generally send requests to the Uptime endpoint at `/v2/uptime/`.

## List All Checks

<a id="opIduptime_checks_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/uptime/checks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/uptime/checks`

To list all of the Uptime checks on your account, send a GET request to `/v2/uptime/checks`.

<h3 id="list-all-checks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "checks": [
    {
      "id": "5a4981aa-9653-4bd1-bef5-d6bff52042e4",
      "enabled": true,
      "name": "Landing page check",
      "regions": [
        "us_east",
        "eu_west"
      ],
      "target": "https://www.landingpage.com",
      "type": "https"
    }
  ],
  "links": {
```

## Create a New Check

<a id="opIduptime_check_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/uptime/checks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "enabled": true,
    "name": "Landing page check",
    "regions": [
      "us_east",
      "eu_west"
    ],
    "target": "https://www.landingpage.com",
    "type": "https"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/uptime/checks`

To create an Uptime check, send a POST request to `/v2/uptime/checks` specifying the attributes
in the table below in the JSON body.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "name": "Landing page check",
  "regions": [
    "us_east",
    "eu_west"
  ],
  "target": "https://www.landingpage.com",
  "type": "https"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» enabled|body|boolean|true|A boolean value indicating whether the check is enabled/disabled.|
|» name|body|string|true|A human-friendly display name.|
|» regions|body|[string]|true|An array containing the selected regions to perform healthchecks from.|
|» target|body|string(url)|true|The endpoint to perform healthchecks on.|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of health check to perform.|

|» type|https|

## Update a Check

<a id="opIduptime_check_update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/uptime/checks/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "enabled": true,
    "name": "Landing page check",
    "regions": [
      "us_east",
      "eu_west"
    ],
    "target": "https://www.landingpage.com",
    "type": "https"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/uptime/checks/{check_id}`

To update the settings of an Uptime check, send a PUT request to `/v2/uptime/checks/$CHECK_ID`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "name": "Landing page check",
  "regions": [
    "us_east",

  "target": "https://www.landingpage.com",
  "type": "https"
}
```

## Delete a Check

<a id="opIduptime_check_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/uptime/checks/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6 \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/uptime/checks/{check_id}`

To delete an Uptime check, send a DELETE request to `/v2/uptime/checks/$CHECK_ID`. A 204 status
code with no body will be returned in response to a successful request.


Deleting a check will also delete alerts associated with the check.


<h3 id="delete-a-check-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|check_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a check.|

```json
}
```

`GET /v2/uptime/checks/{check_id}/alerts`

## Create a New Alert

<a id="opIduptime_alert_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/uptime/checks/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6/alerts \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "comparison": "greater_than",
    "name": "Landing page degraded performance",
    "notifications": {
      "email": [
        "bob@example.com"
      ],
      "slack": [
        {
          "channel": "Production Alerts",
          "url": "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T1234567/AAAAAAAA/ZZZZZZ"
        }
      ]
    },
    "period": "2m",
    "threshold": 300,
    "type": "latency"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/uptime/checks/{check_id}/alerts`

To create an Uptime alert, send a POST request to `/v2/uptime/checks/$CHECK_ID/alerts` specifying the attributes
in the table below in the JSON body.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comparison": "greater_than",
  "name": "Landing page degraded performance",
  "notifications": {
    "email": [
      "bob@example.com"
    ],
    "slack": [
      {
        "channel": "Production Alerts",
        "url": "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T1234567/AAAAAAAA/ZZZZZZ"
      }
    ]
  },
  "period": "2m",
  "threshold": 300,
  "type": "latency"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-alert-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|check_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a check.|
|body|body|object|true|The ''type'' field dictates the type of alert, and hence what type of value to pass into the threshold property.<br>Type \| Description \| Threshold Value<br>-----\|-------------\|--------------------<br>`latency` \| alerts on the response latency \| milliseconds<br>`down` \| alerts on a target registering as down in any region \| N/A (Not required)<br>`down_global` \| alerts on a target registering as down globally \| N/A (Not required)<br>`ssl_expiry` \| alerts on a SSL certificate expiring within $threshold days \| days<br>|
|» comparison|body|string|false|The comparison operator used against the alert's threshold.|
|» name|body|string|true|A human-friendly display name.|
|» notifications|body|object|true|The notification settings for a trigger alert.|
|» » email|body|[string]|true|An email to notify on an alert trigger.|
|» » slack|body|[object]|true|Slack integration details.|
|» » » channel|body|string(string)|true|Slack channel to notify of an alert trigger.|
|» » » url|body|string(string)|true|Slack Webhook URL.|
|» period|body|string|false|Period of time the threshold must be exceeded to trigger the alert.|
|» threshold|body|integer|false|The threshold at which the alert will enter a trigger state. The specific threshold is dependent on the alert type.|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of alert.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» comparison|greater_than|
|» comparison|less_than|
|» period|2m|
|» period|3m|
|» period|5m|
|» period|10m|
|» period|15m|
|» period|30m|
|» period|1h|
|» type|latency|
|» type|down|
|» type|down_global|
|» type|ssl_expiry|

<a id="opIduptime_alert_update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/uptime/checks/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6/alerts/17f0f0ae-b7e5-4ef6-86e3-aa569db58284 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "comparison": "greater_than",
    "name": "Landing page degraded performance",
    "notifications": {
      "email": [
        "bob@example.com"
      ],
      "slack": [
        {
          "channel": "Production Alerts",
          "url": "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T1234567/AAAAAAAA/ZZZZZZ"
        }
      ]
    },
    "period": "2m",
    "threshold": 300,
    "type": "latency"
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/uptime/checks/{check_id}/alerts/{alert_id}`

To update the settings of an Uptime alert, send a PUT request to `/v2/uptime/checks/$CHECK_ID/alerts/$ALERT_ID`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "comparison": "greater_than",
  "name": "Landing page degraded performance",
  "notifications": {
    "email": [
      "bob@example.com"
    ],
    "slack": [
      {
        "channel": "Production Alerts",
        "url": "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T1234567/AAAAAAAA/ZZZZZZ"
      }
    ]
  },
  "period": "2m",
  "threshold": 300,
  "type": "latency"
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-alert-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|check_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a check.|
|alert_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for an alert.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» comparison|body|string|false|The comparison operator used against the alert's threshold.|
|» name|body|string|false|A human-friendly display name.|
|» notifications|body|object|false|The notification settings for a trigger alert.|
|» » email|body|[string]|true|An email to notify on an alert trigger.|
|» » slack|body|[object]|true|Slack integration details.|
|» » » channel|body|string(string)|true|Slack channel to notify of an alert trigger.|
|» » » url|body|string(string)|true|Slack Webhook URL.|
|» period|body|string|false|Period of time the threshold must be exceeded to trigger the alert.|
|» threshold|body|integer|false|The threshold at which the alert will enter a trigger state. The specific threshold is dependent on the alert type.|
|» type|body|string|false|The type of alert.|

<h1 id="digitalocean-api-vpcs">VPCs</h1>

[VPCs (virtual private clouds)](https://www.digitalocean.com/docs/networking/vpc/)
allow you to create virtual networks containing resources that can
communicate with each other in full isolation using private IP addresses.

By sending requests to the `/v2/vpcs` endpoint, you can create, configure,
list, and delete custom VPCs as well as retrieve information about the
resources assigned to them.

## List All VPCs

<a id="opIdvpcs_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/vpcs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/vpcs`

To list all of the VPCs on your account, send a GET request to `/v2/vpcs`.

## Create a New VPC

<a id="opIdvpcs_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/vpcs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "VPC for production environment",
    "name": "env.prod-vpc",
    "ip_range": "10.10.10.0/24",
    "region": "nyc1"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/vpcs`

To create a VPC, send a POST request to `/v2/vpcs` specifying the attributes
in the table below in the JSON body.

**Note:** If you do not currently have a VPC network in a specific datacenter
region, the first one that you create will be set as the default for that
region. The default VPC for a region cannot be changed or deleted.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "VPC for production environment",
  "name": "env.prod-vpc",
  "ip_range": "10.10.10.0/24",
  "region": "nyc1"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-vpc-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|A free-form text field for describing the VPC's purpose. It may be a maximum of 255 characters.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the VPC. Must be unique and may only contain alphanumeric characters, dashes, and periods.|
|» ip_range|body|string|false|The range of IP addresses in the VPC in CIDR notation. Network ranges cannot overlap with other networks in the same account and must be in range of private addresses as defined in RFC1918. It may not be smaller than `/28` nor larger than `/16`. If no IP range is specified, a `/20` network range is generated that won't conflict with other VPC networks in your account.|
|» region|body|string|true|The slug identifier for the region where the VPC will be created.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "vpc": {
    "description": "VPC for production environment",
    "name": "env.prod-vpc",
    "ip_range": "10.10.10.0/24",
    "region": "nyc1",
    "default": true,
    "created_at": "2020-03-13T19:20:47.442049222Z",
    "id": "5a4981aa-9653-4bd1-bef5-d6bff52042e4",
    "urn": "do:droplet:13457723"
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-vpc-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The response will be a JSON object with a key called `vpc`. The value of this will be an object that contains the standard attributes associated with a VPC.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|API Rate limit exceeded|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server error.|Inline|
|default|Default|Unexpected error|Inline|

## Retrieve an Existing VPC

<a id="opIdvpcs_get"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/vpcs/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/vpcs/{vpc_id}`

To show information about an existing VPC, send a GET request to `/v2/vpcs/$VPC_ID`.

<h3 id="retrieve-an-existing-vpc-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|vpc_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a VPC.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

## Update a VPC

<a id="opIdvpcs_update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/vpcs/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "VPC for production environment",
    "name": "env.prod-vpc",
    "default": true
  }'
```

`PUT /v2/vpcs/{vpc_id}`

To update information about a VPC, send a PUT request to `/v2/vpcs/$VPC_ID`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "VPC for production environment",
  "name": "env.prod-vpc",
  "default": true
}
```

|body|body|object|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|A free-form text field for describing the VPC's purpose. It may be a maximum of 255 characters.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the VPC. Must be unique and may only contain alphanumeric characters, dashes, and periods.|
|» default|body|boolean|false|A boolean value indicating whether or not the VPC is the default network for the region. All applicable resources are placed into the default VPC network unless otherwise specified during their creation. The `default` field cannot be unset from `true`. If you want to set a new default VPC network, update the `default` field of another VPC network in the same region. The previous network's `default` field will be set to `false` when a new default VPC has been defined.|

## Delete a VPC

<a id="opIdvpcs_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/vpcs/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /v2/vpcs/{vpc_id}`

To delete a VPC, send a DELETE request to `/v2/vpcs/$VPC_ID`. A 204 status
code with no body will be returned in response to a successful request.

The default VPC for a region can not be deleted. Additionally, a VPC can only
be deleted if it does not contain any member resources. Attempting to delete
a region's default VPC or a VPC that still has members will result in a
403 Forbidden error response.


<h3 id="delete-a-vpc-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|vpc_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a VPC.|

## Partially Update a VPC

<a id="opIdvpcs_patch"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/vpcs/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6 \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "VPC for production environment",
    "name": "env.prod-vpc",
    "default": true
  }'
```

`PATCH /v2/vpcs/{vpc_id}`

To update a subset of information about a VPC, send a PATCH request to
`/v2/vpcs/$VPC_ID`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "VPC for production environment",
  "name": "env.prod-vpc",
  "default": true
}
```

<h3 id="partially-update-a-vpc-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|vpc_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a VPC.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|A free-form text field for describing the VPC's purpose. It may be a maximum of 255 characters.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name of the VPC. Must be unique and may only contain alphanumeric characters, dashes, and periods.|
|» default|body|boolean|false|A boolean value indicating whether or not the VPC is the default network for the region. All applicable resources are placed into the default VPC network unless otherwise specified during their creation. The `default` field cannot be unset from `true`. If you want to set a new default VPC network, update the `default` field of another VPC network in the same region. The previous network's `default` field will be set to `false` when a new default VPC has been defined.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "vpc": {
    "description": "VPC for production environment",
    "name": "env.prod-vpc",
    "ip_range": "10.10.10.0/24",
    "region": "nyc1",
    "default": true,
    "created_at": "2020-03-13T19:20:47.442049222Z",
    "id": "5a4981aa-9653-4bd1-bef5-d6bff52042e4",
    "urn": "do:droplet:13457723"
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "id": "unauthorized",
  "message": "Unable to authenticate you."
}
```

> 404 Response

```json

  "id": "not_found",
  "message": "The resource you requested could not be found."
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "id": "too_many_requests",
  "message": "API Rate limit exceeded."
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "id": "server_error",
  "message": "Unexpected server-side error"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "id": "example_error",
  "message": "some error message"
}
```

## List the Member Resources of a VPC

<a id="opIdvpcs_list_members"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/v2/vpcs/4de7ac8b-495b-4884-9a69-1050c6793cd6/members \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /v2/vpcs/{vpc_id}/members`

To list all of the resources that are members of a VPC, send a GET request to
`/v2/vpcs/$VPC_ID/members`.

To only list resources of a specific type that are members of the VPC,
included a `resource_type` query parameter. For example, to only list Droplets
in the VPC, send a GET request to `/v2/vpcs/$VPC_ID/members?resource_type=droplet`.


<h3 id="list-the-member-resources-of-a-vpc-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|vpc_id|path|string(uuid)|true|A unique identifier for a VPC.|
|resource_type|query|string|false|Used to filter VPC members by a resource type.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of items returned per page|
|page|query|integer|false|Which 'page' of paginated results to return.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "links": {},
  "members": [
    {
      "created_at": "2020-03-13T19:30:48Z",
      "name": "nyc1-load-balancer-01",
      "urn": "do:loadbalancer:fb294d78-d193-4cb2-8737-ea620993591b"
    },
    {
      "created_at": "2020-03-13T19:30:18Z",
      "name": "db-postgresql-nyc1-55986",
      "urn": "do:dbaas:13f7a2f6-43df-4c4a-8129-8733267ddeea"
    },
    {

      "name": "k8s-nyc1-1584127772221",
      "urn": "do:kubernetes:da39d893-96e1-4e4d-971d-1fdda33a46b1"
    },
    {
      "created_at": "2020-03-13T19:29:20Z",
      "name": "ubuntu-s-1vcpu-1gb-nyc1-01",
      "urn": "do:droplet:86e29982-03a7-4946-8a07-a0114dff8754"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "total": 4
  }
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
}
```
